大規模言語モデル(LLM)は単発の指示には強い一方、対話が長引くにつれて初期の指示や設定を取りこぼす傾向がある。本論文はこの現象を「アテンション閉塞(attention closing)」と呼び、注意機構の振る舞いから定量的に分析している。

著者らは複数ターンにわたる対話タスクを設計し、各ターンでモデルが過去のどのトークンに注意を向けているかを層・ヘッド単位で可視化した。その結果、ターン数が増えるほど注意が直近のユーザー発話や特定の「シンク」トークン(BOSや句読点など)に偏り、初期のシステムプロンプトやタスク指示への注意重みが急速に減衰することが示された。これにより、モデルは形式的には会話を続けられても、本来守るべき制約や役割設定を逸脱しやすくなる。

背景として、近年「attention sink」現象(Xiao et al. のStreamingLLMなど)が知られており、初期トークンに不均衡に注意が集中することがロングコンテキスト推論の安定化に寄与する一方、意味的な参照を妨げる副作用も指摘されてきた。本研究はその副作用がマルチターン設定で顕著化することを示した点に新規性があると見られる。

関連する研究動向としては、Anthropicやスタンフォードのグループが報告してきた「lost in the middle」問題、長文脈での指示忠実度低下、さらにシステムプロンプトの強度を維持するためのプロンプトリフレッシュやキャッシュ再投入などの実務的対策がある。本論文の知見は、単にコンテキスト長を拡張するだけでは不十分で、注意分布そのものを設計対象とすべきだという示唆を与える可能性がある。

実装面では、RoPEスケーリング、アテンションテンパリング、明示的なリマインダー挿入などが検討対象となり得る。エージェント開発や長時間のカスタマーサポート用途では、こうした閉塞現象の理解が信頼性向上の鍵となりそうだ。
entries.bodyEn:
Large language models excel at one-shot instructions but tend to drift away from their initial role, constraints, or task definition as a conversation extends across many turns. This paper frames the problem as 'attention closing': a measurable shift in the attention distribution that gradually cuts the model off from its earlier context.

The authors construct multi-turn dialogue benchmarks and inspect, layer by layer and head by head, where the model actually looks when generating each new response. They report that as the number of turns grows, attention concentrates increasingly on the most recent user turn and on a handful of 'sink' tokens such as the BOS marker or punctuation, while the weight assigned to the original system prompt and early task instructions decays sharply. The model can still produce fluent replies, but it becomes more likely to violate constraints, forget persona details, or contradict earlier commitments.

This builds on a growing literature about attention sinks, popularized by work like StreamingLLM from Xiao and colleagues, which showed that LLMs allocate disproportionate attention to initial tokens and that preserving this behavior stabilizes long-context decoding. The trade-off has been noted before: sinks help numerical stability but can also crowd out semantically meaningful references. The contribution here is to show that this side effect is not merely theoretical but actively degrades multi-turn instruction following.

The findings connect naturally to the well-known 'lost in the middle' phenomenon documented by Stanford researchers, in which information placed in the middle of a long context is retrieved less reliably than information at the edges. They also resonate with practitioner reports that system prompts 'wear off' over long agent sessions, prompting workarounds such as periodically reinjecting the system message, using prompt caching with refreshed anchors, or summarizing earlier turns into a compact memory.

If the analysis holds up under replication, it suggests that simply extending context windows, now routinely advertised at hundreds of thousands or even millions of tokens, may not be sufficient on its own. The attention distribution itself appears to be a design surface that deserves explicit engineering. Candidate mitigations include attention temperature scaling, adjusted RoPE or position interpolation schemes, training objectives that penalize over-concentration on sink tokens, and architectural ideas such as register tokens or routing mechanisms that preserve a dedicated channel for high-priority instructions.

For builders of agents, customer-support assistants, and other systems that rely on long-running conversations, this line of research is likely to matter in practice. Reliability over a 50-turn interaction is a different problem than reliability on a single prompt, and benchmarks that average over short tasks may obscure the degradation. Treating attention closing as a first-class failure mode, alongside hallucination and prompt injection, could become standard in future evaluation suites. The paper stops short of proposing a definitive fix, but it offers a useful diagnostic lens that may inform both training-time and inference-time interventions in the coming year.

image.alt: When Attention Closes: How LLMs Lose the Thread in Multi-Turn Interaction

entries.title: Sustaining AI safety: Control-theoretic external impossibility, intrinsic necessity, and structural requirements
entries.titleJa: 制御理論で示すAI安全性の外的不可能性と内在的必要条件
entries.titleEn: Sustaining AI safety: Control-theoretic external impossibility, intrinsic necessity, and structural requirements
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は制御理論の観点からAI安全性を分析し、外部からの完全な制御は不可能であると主張する。安全性を維持するにはAI自身に内在する構造的要件が必要であり、設計段階での組み込みが鍵になると論じている。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.12963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable, safety strategies must be evaluated not only by how much they reduce present risk, but by whether they could
entries.bodyJa:
AIの安全性をいかに持続させるかという問いに対し、本論文は制御理論の枠組みを用いた新しい視座を提示している。著者らは、外部からの監視・制御だけでAIの安全性を保証することは原理的に不可能であると主張し、AI自身の内部構造に安全性を組み込む必要性を論じる。

論文の中心的な議論は、フィードバック制御や可制御性・可観測性といった古典的制御理論の概念をAIシステムに適用する点にある。外部のガードレールやモニタリング、RLHFのような事後的アライメント手法は、観測可能性や応答帯域の制約により、十分に高度なAIシステムを完全には抑え込めない可能性がある。これを著者らは「外的不可能性 (external impossibility)」と呼ぶ。

その上で、安全性を維持するためには内在的必要条件 (intrinsic necessity) が存在すると論じる。すなわち、AIが自身の状態や行動を自己観測し、安全制約を内部の目的関数や構造の中に組み込む仕組みが不可欠だという主張である。これは、Anthropicの Constitutional AI や OpenAI のスーパーアライメント研究、あるいは Stuart Russell が提唱する「目的の不確実性」を組み込む設計思想とも通じる方向性と見られる。

関連分野としては、サイバネティクスや安全工学における Fail-safe 設計、Ashby の必要多様性の法則などが想起される。制御理論をAI安全性に持ち込む試み自体は新しくないが、外的制御の限界を不可能性定理に近い形で定式化し、構造的要件として整理しようとする点に本論文の特徴があると考えられる。実装可能性や定量的検証については今後の課題となる可能性が高い。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper offers a control-theoretic perspective on one of the central questions in AI safety: how can safety be sustained over time as AI systems grow more capable? The authors argue that external oversight alone is fundamentally insufficient, and that safety must be built into the intrinsic structure of the system itself.

The core argument leverages classical concepts from control theory, including feedback, controllability, and observability. When applied to advanced AI, these notions suggest that any purely external controller faces hard limits set by the bandwidth of observation and the speed of intervention. Guardrails, monitoring layers, and post-hoc alignment techniques such as RLHF may therefore be inadequate against a sufficiently capable system. The authors frame this as an external impossibility result, evoking the spirit of classical impossibility theorems in control and computation.

From this negative result, the paper derives a positive claim: an intrinsic necessity. To remain safe, an AI system must internally observe its own state, represent safety constraints within its objective or architecture, and possess structural properties that make unsafe trajectories dynamically unreachable rather than merely discouraged. The authors enumerate what they describe as structural requirements that any sustainably safe AI would need to satisfy.

This line of thinking resonates with several active research threads. Anthropic's Constitutional AI embeds normative constraints directly into training, while OpenAI's now-disbanded superalignment effort sought scalable oversight mechanisms. Stuart Russell's proposal that AI should maintain uncertainty over human objectives similarly tries to bake humility into the system's structure rather than impose it from outside. The current paper can be read as a control-theoretic formalization of intuitions shared across these programs.

There is also a longer intellectual lineage worth noting. Cybernetics, beginning with Wiener and Ashby, treated control and self-regulation as inseparable, and Ashby's law of requisite variety already implies that a controller must match the complexity of the system it governs. Safety engineering traditions around fail-safe design, defense in depth, and inherent safety in nuclear and chemical plants likewise emphasize structural rather than supervisory guarantees. Viewed against this background, the paper's contribution lies less in the intuition that internal safety matters and more in attempting to express the limits of external control as a near-impossibility statement.

Several caveats are worth flagging. The argument appears to be largely conceptual, and translating control-theoretic notions like observability into the messy reality of large neural networks is nontrivial. It remains unclear how the proposed structural requirements would be verified, measured, or enforced during training, and whether they survive distributional shift or self-modification. These concerns are likely to define the agenda for follow-up work.

Still, the framing is useful. As deployed AI systems become more autonomous and operate at speeds that outpace human review, the assumption that an external supervisor can always catch errors looks increasingly fragile. Whether or not one accepts the paper's specific impossibility claim, its insistence that safety be a structural property of the system itself, rather than a property of the surrounding pipeline, aligns with a broader shift in how the field thinks about alignment.

image.alt: Sustaining AI safety: Control-theoretic external impossibility, intrinsic necessity, and structural requirements

entries.title: Position: Agentic AI System Is a Foreseeable Pathway to AGI
entries.titleJa: ポジション論文: エージェント型AIシステムはAGIへの予見可能な道筋である
entries.titleEn: Position: Agentic AI System Is a Foreseeable Pathway to AGI
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、エージェント型AIシステムが汎用人工知能(AGI)に至る最も見通せる道筋であると主張するポジションペーパーである。LLMを核に計画・記憶・ツール利用などを統合する設計が、自律性と汎化能力を段階的に高めると論じる。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.12966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Is monolithic scaling the only path to AGI? This paper challenges the dogma that purely scaling a single model is sufficient to achieve Artificial Gener
entries.bodyJa:
本稿はarXivに投稿されたポジション論文で、エージェント型AIシステム(Agentic AI System)がAGIへ至る最も現実的かつ予見可能な道筋であるとの立場を表明している。著者らは、単体の大規模言語モデル(LLM)が示す能力には限界がある一方、計画立案、長期記憶、ツール利用、自己反省といったコンポーネントを統合した「エージェント」構成が、汎化能力と自律性を段階的に高めうると論じている。

論文の中心的な主張は、AGIを一足飛びに実現する単一アーキテクチャを追うのではなく、既存のLLMを基盤とした多層的なエージェント設計の漸進的進化に注目すべきだという点にある。LLMが推論エンジンとして働き、外部APIやコード実行環境、検索ツール、他のエージェントとの協調を介して、開放的なタスク領域で意思決定を行う構造が、AGIに求められる汎用性に近づく鍵だと位置づけている。

背景として、2023年以降の業界では AutoGPT や BabyAGI といった初期のエージェント実装に始まり、OpenAI の Assistants API、Anthropic の Computer Use、Google の Project Astra、Microsoft の AutoGen、LangGraph や CrewAI などのフレームワーク群が登場しており、エージェント化はLLM活用の主要な発展方向となっている。本論文の主張はこうした産業動向とも整合的だと見られる。

一方で、エージェント型のアプローチがAGIに到達するかは依然として議論が分かれている。Yann LeCun のように自己回帰型LLMの根本的限界を指摘し、世界モデルベースのアーキテクチャを推す立場や、強化学習主導の経路を重視する研究者も存在する。また、エージェントの自律性が高まるほど、安全性・整合性・誤作動リスクの管理が難しくなる可能性があり、評価指標やガバナンスの整備も今後の課題となるだろう。本論文はそうした論点を含め、研究コミュニティに議論の出発点を提示するものといえる。
entries.bodyEn:
This arXiv position paper argues that agentic AI systems represent the most foreseeable pathway toward artificial general intelligence (AGI). Rather than expecting AGI to emerge from a single monolithic model, the authors contend that integrating large language models with planning, memory, tool use, and self-reflection mechanisms is the practical route by which autonomy and generalization will progressively expand.

At the heart of the argument lies a shift in framing. A standalone LLM, however capable, exhibits clear limitations in long-horizon reasoning, persistent state, and grounded action. When wrapped inside an agentic architecture—where the model acts as a reasoning core coordinating external APIs, code execution, retrieval, and other agents—it begins to exhibit broader, more open-ended problem-solving behavior. The authors view this layered composition as the substrate from which AGI-like generality could incrementally emerge.

The position aligns with strong industry momentum. Since the early experiments with AutoGPT and BabyAGI in 2023, agent frameworks have proliferated: OpenAI's Assistants and Responses APIs, Anthropic's Computer Use, Google's Project Astra, Microsoft's AutoGen, and open-source orchestration libraries like LangGraph and CrewAI. Enterprise deployments increasingly center on multi-agent workflows rather than single-shot prompting, suggesting that the agentic paradigm is already the de facto direction of applied LLM research.

Still, whether this path genuinely leads to AGI remains contested. Yann LeCun and others have argued that autoregressive LLMs are fundamentally limited and that world-model-based architectures, possibly trained with objectives beyond next-token prediction, will be required. Reinforcement-learning-centric researchers emphasize embodied or environment-driven learning loops. From this perspective, agentic scaffolding could be seen as a useful engineering layer but not a sufficient condition for general intelligence.

There are also significant safety considerations. As agents acquire tool use, persistent memory, and the ability to spawn or coordinate with other agents, the surface area for misalignment, prompt injection, runaway behavior, and cascading errors grows correspondingly. Evaluation methodologies for agentic systems remain immature—benchmarks like GAIA, SWE-bench, and OSWorld are emerging, but capturing open-ended general capability is still an unsolved problem. Governance frameworks, including those proposed under the EU AI Act and various national AI safety institutes, are only beginning to grapple with autonomous agents specifically.

The paper's contribution is best understood not as empirical proof but as a framing document. By explicitly positioning agentic systems as a foreseeable AGI pathway, it invites the research community to debate which architectural ingredients are necessary, which are sufficient, and how progress should be measured. Readers should treat the claim as a hypothesis to interrogate rather than a settled conclusion, particularly given how rapidly the agent ecosystem—and critiques of it—continue to evolve.

image.alt: Position: Agentic AI System Is a Foreseeable Pathway to AGI

entries.title: Retrieval is Cheap, Show Me the Code: Executable Multi-Hop Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entries.titleJa: 検索より実行を重視するRAG向け多段推論フレームワーク
entries.titleEn: Retrieval is Cheap, Show Me the Code: Executable Multi-Hop Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、Retrieval-Augmented Generation(RAG)における多段推論を、自然言語ではなく実行可能コードとして表現する新手法を提案する。検索コストを抑えつつ、複雑な質問に対する推論の精度と透明性を高める狙いがある。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.12975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a standard approach for knowledge-intensive question answering, but existing systems remain brittle on m
entries.bodyJa:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation(RAG)は、外部知識を取り込みながら大規模言語モデル(LLM)に回答させる定番手法として広く普及している。本論文はそのRAGにおける「多段推論(multi-hop reasoning)」を、自然言語の思考連鎖ではなく実行可能なコードとして表現する新しいフレームワークを提案している。

従来のRAGでは、複雑な質問に答えるためにChain-of-Thoughtのような自然言語ベースの推論ステップを生成し、その都度ドキュメントを検索して回答を構築する方法が一般的だった。しかしこの方式では、推論の途中経過が曖昧になりやすく、検索の呼び出し回数が増えてコストや遅延が膨らむという課題が指摘されてきた。著者らは「検索は安い、コードを見せろ」という挑発的なタイトルが示すように、検索量を増やすのではなく、推論プロセス自体を構造化されたコードに落とし込むことで効率と精度の両立を狙う。

具体的には、LLMに対し質問を分解する手順をプログラムとして生成させ、関数呼び出しや変数を介して中間結果を引き渡しながら、必要なタイミングで検索APIを実行する枠組みと見られる。これにより、各推論ステップが明示的かつ検証可能になり、誤った中間結果の混入や幻覚の連鎖を抑えやすくなる可能性がある。

関連する潮流として、Program-aided Language Models(PAL)やReAct、LangChainのエージェント機能、OpenAIのfunction callingなど、LLMにコード生成と外部ツール利用を組み合わせる研究・実装が急速に増えている。本研究もこの「コードを推論の中間表現とする」流れに位置付けられ、HotpotQAやMuSiQueといった多段QAベンチマークでの評価が想定される。RAG運用におけるコスト最適化と説明可能性の両面で、実務応用への示唆を持つ研究と言える。
entries.bodyEn:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a default pattern for grounding large language models in external knowledge, but handling complex, multi-hop questions remains a stubborn problem. This paper argues that the bottleneck is no longer retrieval itself, which has become cheap and fast, but the way reasoning over retrieved evidence is expressed and executed.

The authors propose representing multi-hop reasoning as executable code rather than as a natural-language chain of thought. In conventional RAG pipelines, an LLM produces a free-form reasoning trace, issues retrieval calls along the way, and composes a final answer. While flexible, this approach tends to drift: intermediate conclusions are vague, error propagation is hard to detect, and the system often makes redundant retrieval calls that inflate latency and cost without improving accuracy.

By contrast, a code-centric formulation forces the model to decompose a question into discrete operations, with explicit variables, function calls, and control flow. Retrieval becomes a callable tool invoked at well-defined points, and intermediate results are first-class values that can be inspected, reused, or validated. The provocative framing in the title—retrieval is cheap, show me the code—captures the shift in emphasis: spend less effort on issuing more queries, and more on structuring how evidence is combined.

This approach is likely to deliver several practical benefits. Reasoning traces become auditable, which matters for enterprise deployments where explainability is a hard requirement. Errors can be localized to specific steps rather than buried in prose. And because the program structure makes data dependencies explicit, the system can in principle parallelize independent retrievals or cache intermediate results, though the precise engineering details would need to be confirmed from the full paper.

The work fits within a broader movement to treat code as a universal intermediate representation for LLM reasoning. Program-aided Language Models (PAL), Toolformer, ReAct-style agents, and the function-calling interfaces now standard in OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-source toolkits all push in the same direction. Frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, and DSPy have begun exposing structured pipelines that resemble compiled programs more than free-form prompts. Code-as-reasoning approaches have also shown strong results on math and symbolic benchmarks, and extending them to retrieval-heavy QA is a natural next step.

For multi-hop question answering specifically, datasets like HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue have long exposed the weakness of single-shot retrieval plus naive prompting. Iterative retrieval methods such as IRCoT and Self-Ask improved matters by interleaving search and reasoning, but they still rely on natural-language glue. A code-based formulation could be seen as the logical endpoint of that trajectory, trading some generative flexibility for determinism and inspectability.

There are open questions worth watching. Code generation itself can hallucinate, especially when the schema of available tools is complex, and forcing structure may hurt performance on questions that genuinely benefit from associative reasoning. The trade-off between expressiveness and reliability will likely depend on domain, model size, and the quality of the tool interface. Still, as RAG systems move from demos into production, approaches that make reasoning legible and debuggable—rather than merely fluent—appear increasingly valuable, and this paper contributes a concrete proposal in that direction.

image.alt: Retrieval is Cheap, Show Me the Code: Executable Multi-Hop Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

entries.title: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs
entries.titleJa: LLMによる継続的更新で有用な記憶が誤りに変質する現象
entries.titleEn: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs
entries.summaryJa: 本研究は、LLMエージェントが長期記憶を継続的に書き換えると、当初は正確だった有用な記憶が次第に歪み誤情報化することを示す。検索拡張やメモリ機構の信頼性に課題を投げかける知見である。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.12978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning from past experience benefits from two complementary forms of memory: episodic traces -- raw trajectories of what happened -- and consolidated
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)を用いたエージェントでは、対話履歴やタスク結果を長期記憶として保持し、必要に応じて書き換えながら参照する仕組みが一般化しつつある。本論文は、この「継続的な記憶更新」が思わぬ副作用をもたらすことを実験的に示した。

著者らは、当初は正確で有用だった記憶エントリが、LLM自身による要約・統合・書き換えを繰り返すうちに少しずつ歪み、最終的には誤情報や矛盾した内容へと劣化していく現象を観察したと報告している。これは、人間の記憶における「再固定化(reconsolidation)」に似た過程とも言え、想起のたびに情報が再構成される過程で誤差が蓄積していくと見られる。

技術的背景としては、LangChainやLlamaIndex、近年のMem0やLetta(旧MemGPT)など、エージェントに永続的メモリを与えるフレームワークが急速に普及している点が挙げられる。これらは通常、ベクトル検索による意味的想起と、LLMによる要約圧縮を組み合わせる。問題は、圧縮や統合のステップにLLMの生成的なゆらぎが介在することで、忠実性が保証されない点にある。本研究の知見は、長期運用するパーソナルアシスタントやマルチエージェントシステムにおいて、記憶の品質保証が独立した研究課題であることを浮き彫りにする。

対策としては、原文の不変保存と派生サマリの分離、出典トレーサビリティの確保、定期的な検証ステップ、信頼度スコアの付与などが考えられるが、いずれも計算コストと精度のトレードオフを伴う可能性がある。検索拡張生成(RAG)が主流化する中で、「読み取り専用の知識ベース」と「書き換え可能なエージェントメモリ」の設計上の役割分担を明確にする必要性が改めて示唆されたと言えるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
LLM-powered agents increasingly rely on long-term memory: they store conversation history and task outcomes, rewrite or summarize them over time, and retrieve them when relevant. This paper provides an empirical look at an underappreciated failure mode of that paradigm, showing that the very act of continuously updating memory tends to corrupt it.

The authors report that memory entries which start out accurate and useful gradually drift as the LLM repeatedly summarizes, merges, and rewrites them. Over many update cycles, factual details get blurred, context is lost, and entries eventually contain misleading or contradictory content. The dynamic is reminiscent of memory reconsolidation in human cognition, where each act of recall slightly rewrites the trace and small errors compound over time.

The finding lands in a moment when persistent-memory frameworks for agents are proliferating. Tools such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, Mem0, and Letta (formerly MemGPT) combine vector retrieval for semantic recall with LLM-driven summarization for compression. The compression step is convenient but introduces generative variance: there is no guarantee that the rewritten memory remains faithful to the original observation. For long-running personal assistants, customer-support bots, or multi-agent simulations, this suggests that memory quality assurance is becoming a research problem in its own right, distinct from retrieval quality or model capability.

Possible mitigations include preserving raw observations immutably while keeping derived summaries as separate, regenerable artifacts; maintaining provenance links so any claim can be traced back to its source; running periodic verification passes that re-check stored facts against authoritative inputs; and attaching confidence or freshness scores that decay with each rewrite. Each of these, however, likely trades compute and storage cost for fidelity, and the right balance may be application-specific.

More broadly, the work hints at an emerging design principle for retrieval-augmented systems: read-only knowledge bases and writable agent memories should probably play different architectural roles. Treating them interchangeably—letting an LLM freely overwrite its own factual store—appears to invite slow but cumulative degradation. As agentic systems move from demos to production, expect more attention to memory governance, audit trails, and perhaps formal notions of memory integrity, similar to how databases evolved consistency guarantees decades ago.

image.alt: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs

entries.title: Retrieval-Augmented Tutoring for Algorithm Tracing and Problem-Solving in AI Education
entries.titleJa: アルゴリズム理解を支援する検索拡張型AIチュータリング手法
entries.titleEn: Retrieval-Augmented Tutoring for Algorithm Tracing and Problem-Solving in AI Education
entries.summaryJa: AI教育におけるアルゴリズムのトレースや問題解決を支援するため、検索拡張生成(RAG)を活用したチュータリングシステムを提案する研究。学習者の質問に対し教材コンテンツを根拠として回答を生成し、汎用LLMよりも正確で文脈に即した指導を実現することを目指す。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.12988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Students learning algorithms often need support as they interpret traces, debug reasoning errors, and apply procedures across unfamiliar problem instanc
entries.bodyJa:
本研究は、人工知能の授業で扱うアルゴリズムのトレースや問題解決を学習者が習得する際に、検索拡張生成(RAG)を用いたチュータリングシステムが有効であることを示そうとする試みである。AI教育における自動チューターの精度と信頼性向上を目的としており、学習支援分野でのLLM応用例として注目される。

汎用の大規模言語モデルは、A*探索やミニマックス、制約充足など教科書的アルゴリズムの説明を概ねこなせる一方、教師が用いる特定の表記や擬似コード、講義スライド特有の前提条件と齟齬を起こすことが知られている。RAGは外部知識ベース(講義ノート、教科書、過去問など)から関連箇所を検索し、その内容をプロンプトに注入して回答生成に利用するアプローチで、こうした文脈ずれを抑える狙いがある。

本論文はそのアイデアをAI入門コースのチューターに適用し、学生がアルゴリズムの実行ステップを追跡する際の質疑応答や、演習問題の段階的ヒント提示に活かす設計と見られる。教材コーパスを根拠とすることで、ハルシネーションの低減や、教員の教え方への整合性向上が期待される。

関連する動向として、CarnegieやKhan Academyの「Khanmigo」、Courseraのコーチ機能など、教育向けLLMチューターは急速に広がっている。Stanford等の研究でも、ソクラテス式の対話設計や誤答に対するスキャフォールディングが学習効果に寄与すると報告されており、単に正答を返すのではなく学習者の思考を引き出す対話戦略との組み合わせが鍵になる可能性がある。

また、RAGの実装にはベクトル検索(FAISS、Chroma等)や埋め込みモデルの選定、チャンク分割の粒度といった工学的判断が伴う。アルゴリズムのトレースのように記号操作と段階推論が求められるタスクでは、検索結果に加えてChain-of-Thoughtやツール使用(コード実行)を組み合わせる構成も検討余地があると考えられる。なお本論文の評価規模や具体的成果については原文を参照されたい。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper explores how retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can be applied to building tutoring systems for introductory artificial intelligence courses, specifically targeting two notoriously difficult skills for students: tracing the execution of classical algorithms and working through structured problem-solving exercises. The work positions itself within a fast-growing area of educational AI, where large language models are being repurposed as on-demand tutors.

The motivation is well known to anyone who has tried using a general-purpose chatbot for coursework. Models such as GPT-4 or Claude can describe A* search, minimax with alpha-beta pruning, or constraint satisfaction in broad strokes, but their explanations frequently diverge from the specific notation, pseudocode conventions, or simplifying assumptions used in a given lecture. Students who follow the model's variant may end up confused when graded against the instructor's version. RAG addresses this by retrieving passages from a curated corpus, typically lecture notes, textbook chapters, and past problem sets, and injecting them into the model's context so that answers stay anchored to the course's own framing.

Applied to algorithm tracing, this approach is particularly attractive. Tracing requires step-by-step symbolic manipulation: maintaining an open list, updating heuristic values, or unfolding a recursion. Retrieval can supply the exact algorithm definition the instructor uses, while the model handles the reasoning. The authors appear to design their system around this division of labor, though specifics of evaluation scale and learning outcomes should be read from the paper itself.

The broader ecosystem context is worth noting. Khan Academy's Khanmigo, Coursera Coach, and various university pilots have demonstrated growing appetite for LLM tutors, while research from groups at Stanford and CMU suggests that Socratic dialogue, scaffolding, and well-calibrated hints matter more for learning gains than raw answer accuracy. A RAG tutor that simply produces correct solutions may not maximize learning; combining grounded retrieval with pedagogical strategies that elicit student reasoning is likely a more promising direction.

From an engineering standpoint, building such a system involves familiar but non-trivial choices: selecting an embedding model, deciding chunk granularity for course materials, and using a vector store such as FAISS, Chroma, or pgvector. For symbolic tasks like algorithm tracing, retrieval alone may be insufficient, and pairing it with chain-of-thought prompting or tool use, for instance executing student code in a sandbox, could plausibly improve reliability. Hallucinations on intermediate states of a search tree are a known failure mode that pure text generation handles poorly.

Overall, the contribution fits a recognizable pattern in current AI-in-education research: take a well-understood retrieval pipeline, apply it carefully to a domain where instructor-specific conventions matter, and study whether students benefit. Whether such systems ultimately outperform thoughtfully designed traditional tutoring, or merely match it at lower cost, remains an open empirical question that the wider community is actively investigating.

image.alt: Retrieval-Augmented Tutoring for Algorithm Tracing and Problem-Solving in AI Education

entries.title: MAP: A Map-then-Act Paradigm for Long-Horizon Interactive Agent Reasoning
entries.titleJa: MAP: 長期対話エージェントのための「地図化してから行動」パラダイム
entries.titleEn: MAP: A Map-then-Act Paradigm for Long-Horizon Interactive Agent Reasoning
entries.summaryJa: 長期的なインタラクティブ推論を行うエージェント向けに、環境を先に「地図化」してから行動するMAPパラダイムを提案。計画と実行を分離し、複雑なタスクでの一貫性と効率を高めることを目指す研究。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current interactive LLM agents rely on goal-conditioned stepwise planning, where environmental understanding is acquired reactively during execution rat
entries.bodyJa:
長期的な対話と意思決定を要するエージェント研究において、計画と実行をどう切り分けるかは依然として中心的課題である。本論文「MAP: A Map-then-Act Paradigm for Long-Horizon Interactive Agent Reasoning」は、エージェントがまず環境構造を「地図化(Map)」し、その後にその地図を参照しながら行動(Act)する二段階パラダイムを提示している。

MAPの基本アイデアは、LLMエージェントが直接ステップごとに反応的に行動するのではなく、観測から得た情報を構造化された内部表現にまとめ、それを長期計画の基盤とする点にある。これにより、深い探索や複数サブゴールを跨ぐタスクでの一貫性が改善されると見られる。従来のReActやReflexionといった手法は思考と行動を交互に挟むが、長期タスクでは履歴の肥大化や文脈の希薄化が課題となっていた。

地図化フェーズでは、空間的・意味的な関係を含む環境モデルを構築し、行動フェーズではその地図に基づき、必要に応じて部分的に再地図化しながらタスクを遂行すると考えられる。これは古典的なロボティクスにおけるSLAMやhierarchical planningの発想を、言語モデル駆動のエージェントに応用したものと位置づけられる。

関連研究としては、Voyager(Minecraftでスキルライブラリを構築)、AutoGPT系の自己計画エージェント、あるいはWebArenaやALFWorldのような長期インタラクション評価ベンチマークが挙げられる。これらに共通する課題は、ステップ数が増えるほど誤りが累積する「ホライゾン問題」であり、MAPはその緩和策として位置づけられる可能性がある。

なお、提示されたURLのIDから判断するに、論文の詳細な実験設定や評価ベンチマーク、ベースライン比較については原典を参照する必要がある。実環境タスクでの汎化性能や、地図表現のスケーラビリティが今後の検証ポイントになると見られる。
entries.bodyEn:
Building agents that can reason and act coherently over long horizons remains one of the harder open problems in LLM research. The paper "MAP: A Map-then-Act Paradigm for Long-Horizon Interactive Agent Reasoning" proposes a two-stage approach in which an agent first constructs an internal map of its environment and then acts against that map, rather than reacting step-by-step from raw observations.

The core intuition is that reactive paradigms like ReAct or Reflexion, while effective on short tasks, tend to accumulate errors and lose context as trajectories grow longer. By front-loading a structured representation of the environment, an agent can ground its subsequent decisions in a more stable substrate. The mapping phase is intended to capture spatial, semantic, and relational structure, while the acting phase consults and possibly updates this map as new information arrives.

This framing borrows conceptually from classical robotics, where SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping) and hierarchical task planning have long separated world modeling from control. Applying the same decomposition to language-model-driven agents is a natural move, and several recent systems gesture in this direction. Voyager builds a reusable skill library in Minecraft; AutoGPT-style systems attempt explicit plan trees; and benchmarks like ALFWorld, WebArena, and ScienceWorld have made the horizon problem measurable. MAP appears to position itself as a more principled response to that problem, though the exact mechanisms and empirical gains would need to be confirmed against the full paper.

A few questions are worth flagging. First, the quality of the map representation likely determines downstream performance: too abstract and it loses actionable detail, too granular and it inherits the same context-bloat issues the paradigm aims to avoid. Second, real environments are partially observable and non-stationary, so a static map is rarely sufficient; the interplay between initial mapping and incremental updates during acting is probably where much of the engineering complexity lives. Third, the cost profile matters. A dedicated mapping pass adds latency and token usage up front, which may pay off on long tasks but could be wasteful on shorter ones, suggesting that adaptive triggering of the map phase could be valuable.

For practitioners, the takeaway is that the field is steadily moving away from monolithic prompt-and-react loops toward more explicit cognitive architectures that separate perception, world modeling, planning, and execution. Whether MAP becomes a widely adopted pattern or a stepping stone toward richer memory-and-planning frameworks will likely depend on how well its gains generalize beyond the benchmarks reported in the paper. Readers interested in the specifics of evaluation, baselines, and ablations should consult the original work, as the broader claims here should be read with appropriate hedging until independently reproduced.

image.alt: MAP: A Map-then-Act Paradigm for Long-Horizon Interactive Agent Reasoning

entries.title: An Agentic LLM-Based Framework for Population-Scale Mental Health Screening
entries.titleJa: LLMエージェントによる集団規模のメンタルヘルススクリーニング基盤
entries.titleEn: An Agentic LLM-Based Framework for Population-Scale Mental Health Screening
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、LLMを活用したエージェント型フレームワークにより、集団規模でのメンタルヘルススクリーニングを行う手法を提案。臨床判断を補助しつつ大量データを処理する仕組みを示し、医療現場での実用化可能性を検討している。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mental health disorders affect millions worldwide, and healthcare systems are increasingly overwhelmed by the volume of clinical data generated from ele
entries.bodyJa:
メンタルヘルスの早期発見は世界的な公衆衛生課題だが、専門家不足と評価コストが障壁となっている。本論文は、大規模言語モデル(LLM)をエージェントとして組み合わせ、集団規模でメンタルヘルススクリーニングを自動化するフレームワークを提案している。

提案手法では、複数のLLMエージェントが役割分担しながら患者データやアンケート回答を解析し、リスクの高い個人を抽出する。単一モデルによる推論ではなく、エージェント間で協調・検証する設計により、誤判定の低減と説明可能性の向上を狙うと見られる。臨床医による最終判断を前提とした「補助ツール」としての位置づけが想定されている。

背景として、PHQ-9やGAD-7など定型化された自己申告スケールが広く使われているが、回答の解釈や追跡には人手が必要で、地域や集団全体をカバーするのは難しい。近年はWoebotやWysaなどLLMやチャットボットを用いた介入サービスも登場しており、Anthropic・OpenAI各社のモデルを基盤に診療支援を試みる研究も増えている。エージェント型アプローチは、AutoGenやLangGraphに代表される協調フレームワークの臨床応用の一例とも位置づけられる。

一方で、メンタルヘルス領域でのLLM活用にはバイアス、プライバシー、誤検知による偽陽性・偽陰性のリスクなど慎重な検討が必要である。本研究の評価範囲や実臨床への展開にあたっては、規制・倫理面のレビューが不可欠と考えられる。論文の詳細な精度や対象データセットについては原文を確認する必要がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Mental health conditions remain underdiagnosed worldwide, largely because clinical assessment is labor-intensive and specialists are in short supply. This paper proposes an agentic framework built on large language models (LLMs) to perform mental health screening at population scale, with the aim of identifying at-risk individuals from large volumes of patient-reported data while keeping clinicians in the loop.

Rather than relying on a single monolithic model, the proposed approach distributes the screening workflow across multiple cooperating LLM agents. Each agent handles a specialized subtask such as parsing responses, cross-checking signals, or producing structured risk assessments. The authors appear to argue that multi-agent coordination improves robustness and interpretability compared with one-shot prompting, although the exact accuracy figures and datasets warrant a direct reading of the paper.

The broader context is worth noting. Standardized self-report instruments like the PHQ-9 for depression and GAD-7 for anxiety are widely used, but interpreting and following up on responses at scale is operationally difficult. Public health systems often struggle to reach entire populations, and digital tools such as Woebot, Wysa, and various telehealth platforms have tried to fill the gap with chatbot-style interventions. Research groups have also been exploring foundation models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-weight providers as decision support, though regulatory clearance for clinical use remains limited.

The agentic angle of this work fits into a wider trend in 2024-2025 where frameworks like AutoGen, LangGraph, and CrewAI have popularized multi-agent orchestration. Applying that pattern to clinical screening is a natural step, but mental health is a particularly sensitive domain. False negatives can leave high-risk individuals undetected, while false positives can cause distress, stigma, or unnecessary clinical workload. Bias against minority groups, language varieties, or culturally specific expressions of distress is another well-documented risk in LLM-based health applications.

Privacy and governance are equally important. Population-scale screening implies processing identifiable health data, which raises HIPAA, GDPR, and local regulatory questions about where inference runs, how prompts are logged, and how model providers handle sensitive content. Any real-world deployment would likely require on-premise or vetted cloud inference, audit trails, and human review at critical decision points.

Readers interested in the technical details, including the agent architecture, evaluation methodology, and any clinical validation, should consult the original paper. The contribution seems most useful as a blueprint for how agentic LLM pipelines might augment, rather than replace, traditional screening workflows, and as a starting point for further discussion on responsible deployment in mental health care.

image.alt: An Agentic LLM-Based Framework for Population-Scale Mental Health Screening

entries.title: GRACE: Gradient-aligned Reasoning Data Curation for Efficient Post-training
entries.titleJa: GRACE: 勾配整合による効率的な事後学習向け推論データキュレーション
entries.titleEn: GRACE: Gradient-aligned Reasoning Data Curation for Efficient Post-training
entries.summaryJa: GRACEは、推論モデルの事後学習で用いる訓練データを勾配の整合性に基づき選別する手法を提案する。冗長または有害なサンプルを除去し、少量データでも高い推論性能を達成することを狙う。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing reasoning data curation pipelines score whole samples, treating every intermediate step as equally valuable. In reality, steps within a trace c
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデルの推論能力を引き上げる事後学習(post-training)では、どのデータで学習させるかが性能を大きく左右する。GRACEは、勾配の整合性(gradient alignment)を指標として推論用訓練データを選別する新たなキュレーション手法を提案する論文である。

GRACEの基本アイデアは、各訓練サンプルが生む勾配が、目標タスクや検証セットの勾配方向とどれだけ揃っているかを評価し、整合性の高いサンプルを優先的に採用するというものだ。これにより、冗長なサンプルや学習を阻害する可能性のあるノイズデータを除外でき、より少ない計算コストで同等以上の推論性能を得ることが期待される。著者らは、推論タスクを対象とした実験で、ランダム選択や従来の難易度ベース選別手法を上回る効率を示したとみられる。

背景として、近年はOpenAI o1やDeepSeek-R1に代表される「推論特化型」モデルの台頭により、Chain-of-Thoughtを含む高品質な推論データの確保が研究コミュニティの焦点になっている。一方で、合成データやWeb由来の推論トレースは品質にばらつきが大きく、単純な大規模化では性能が頭打ちになることが指摘されている。LIMAやs1のように「少数の厳選データでも高い性能が出る」という知見も蓄積されつつあり、GRACEはその系譜に位置づけられる試みと言えるだろう。

関連手法としては、影響関数(influence function)を使ったデータ選別や、DataInf、LESSなど勾配ベースのデータ価値推定の研究が存在する。GRACEはこれらと近いアプローチを取りつつ、推論タスク特有の長い思考連鎖を含むサンプルへの適用を意識している点が新しい可能性がある。実運用上は勾配計算コストが課題となるが、近似手法や層選択により実用域に落とし込めるかが焦点になりそうだ。

なお本稿執筆時点で論文URLには不審点があり、最終的な実験結果や採用ベンチマークの詳細は原文を確認することが望ましい。事後学習データキュレーションは2024〜2025年にかけて急速に研究が進む領域であり、GRACEのような勾配整合アプローチが今後の標準的なベースラインとして定着するかは注目に値する。
entries.bodyEn:
Selecting the right training data has emerged as one of the most consequential decisions in post-training large language models for reasoning. GRACE introduces a gradient-aligned data curation method that scores candidate samples by how well their training gradients align with those of a target objective or validation set, keeping only the most aligned examples for fine-tuning.

The intuition is straightforward: if a sample's gradient points in roughly the same direction as the gradient computed on held-out reasoning tasks, training on it should make consistent progress toward the desired capability. Conversely, samples whose gradients point elsewhere may be redundant, noisy, or actively harmful. By filtering on this signal, GRACE aims to match or exceed the performance of much larger, unfiltered datasets while substantially reducing compute. The authors reportedly show gains over random sampling and difficulty-based baselines on reasoning benchmarks.

The broader context matters. Following the rise of reasoning-focused models like OpenAI's o1 and DeepSeek-R1, the community has shifted attention from raw scale to the quality of chain-of-thought traces used in supervised fine-tuning and RL. Web-scraped or synthetically generated reasoning data is highly variable, and naive scaling often plateaus. Recent results such as LIMA and s1 have demonstrated that a few thousand carefully chosen examples can rival far larger corpora, and GRACE fits squarely into this minimalist, quality-first lineage.

Methodologically, GRACE sits alongside a growing body of gradient-based data valuation work, including influence functions, DataInf, and LESS, which similarly use first-order information to estimate which examples matter most. What may distinguish GRACE is its focus on long-form reasoning traces, where gradient signals must be aggregated across many tokens of intermediate thought rather than short instruction-response pairs. This raises practical questions: per-sample gradient computation is expensive, so the approach likely relies on low-rank approximations, layer subsampling, or projection tricks to remain tractable at scale. Whether those approximations preserve the alignment signal for very long chains of thought is an open empirical question.

There are also methodological caveats worth flagging. Gradient alignment is measured with respect to some reference distribution, and the choice of that reference effectively defines what 'good reasoning data' means. Overfitting the curation signal to a narrow validation set could yield datasets that excel on benchmarks but generalize less well to out-of-distribution problems. Robust evaluation across multiple reasoning suites, ideally including held-out domains, will be important for assessing whether GRACE's gains reflect genuine capability or curation-induced benchmark alignment.

It is worth noting that the provided URL appears unusual, so readers should consult the actual arXiv listing for the definitive experimental setup, datasets, and baselines. Regardless, data curation for post-training is one of the fastest-moving subfields in LLM research right now, and gradient-aligned selection looks poised to become a standard baseline alongside influence-based and embedding-similarity methods. If GRACE's approach generalizes, it could meaningfully reduce the cost of building reasoning-strong open models, an area where both academic labs and companies like Meta, Mistral, and Qwen are competing aggressively.

image.alt: GRACE: Gradient-aligned Reasoning Data Curation for Efficient Post-training

entries.title: A Constraint Programming Approach for $n$-Day Lookahead Playoff Clinching
entries.titleJa: 制約プログラミングによるNデイ先読みのプレーオフ進出判定
entries.titleEn: A Constraint Programming Approach for $n$-Day Lookahead Playoff Clinching
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、スポーツリーグでチームがNデイ先読みでプレーオフ進出を確定できるかを判定する問題に対し、制約プログラミング(CP)を用いたアプローチを提案する。従来のグラフ理論やネットワークフロー手法では扱いにくい複雑なタイブレーク規則や残り試合の組合せ条件を、CPの宣言的モデルで効率的に扱える点が特徴である。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In professional sports, a team has clinched the playoffs if they are guaranteed a postseason spot, regardless of the outcomes of any remaining games. As
entries.bodyJa:
スポーツリーグでチームがプレーオフ進出を「確定」したかどうかを判定する問題は、組合せ最適化の古典的な題材として知られている。本論文は、その判定を残りNデイ(N日先)に限定した先読み版として定式化し、制約プログラミング(Constraint Programming, CP)による解法を提案するものである。

通常のプレーオフ進出判定(clinching)は、最大流・最小カットなどネットワークフロー的な手法で扱われてきた。Schwartz (1966) の研究以来、勝率や残り試合数だけを用いる単純なケースでは多項式時間で解けることが知られている。しかし現実のリーグでは、同率の場合の直接対戦成績、ディビジョン内成績、得失点差といった複雑なタイブレーク規則が階層的に適用され、こうした条件はフローモデルでは表現が難しい。

そこで本研究は、残り日程の各試合結果を変数とし、タイブレーク規則や順位条件を制約として宣言的に記述するCPアプローチを採用したと見られる。Nデイ先読みという設定は、「今後N日以内のどの結果シナリオでも当該チームが進出を確定するか」を問うもので、放送スケジュールやマジックナンバー算定など実務的な需要にも対応する。CPは枝刈りと伝播により探索空間を縮約でき、不規則な制約に対する柔軟性で従来手法を補完する。

関連知見として、メジャーリーグやNBAではマジックナンバーが日々公表されるが、その正確な計算にはタイブレーク全体を考慮する必要があり、近年はMIP(混合整数計画)やSATによる解法も検討されている。OR-ToolsやMiniZincといった汎用CPソルバの成熟により、こうしたスポーツスケジューリング応用は実装コストが下がっている。本論文の貢献は、理論的に難しい部分を実用的なモデリング言語に落とし込んだ点にあると考えられるが、スケーラビリティや実リーグデータでの検証範囲については原文を参照されたい。
entries.bodyEn:
Determining whether a sports team has mathematically clinched a playoff berth is a classic problem in combinatorial optimization. This paper reframes the question with a finite horizon: given the next n days of scheduled games, can we certify that a team is guaranteed a playoff spot regardless of outcomes within that window? The authors propose a constraint programming (CP) formulation to answer it.

The traditional clinching question, dating back to Schwartz's 1966 work, is typically solved via maximum-flow or min-cut reductions when the only criterion is win totals or simple winning percentage. Under that simplified model, polynomial-time algorithms suffice. Real leagues, however, layer on intricate tiebreaker rules: head-to-head records, divisional records, conference records, point differentials, and even coin flips at the bottom of the hierarchy. These conditional, lexicographic rules are awkward to express in a pure network-flow model.

A CP approach sidesteps that limitation by treating each remaining game outcome as a decision variable and encoding standings, tiebreakers, and qualification thresholds as declarative constraints. The n-day lookahead variant is practically motivated: broadcasters, league offices, and fans care about near-term certainty, and magic-number computations implicitly assume some form of lookahead. By bounding the horizon, the search space stays tractable while the model retains the full expressive power needed for realistic rules. CP solvers exploit constraint propagation and learned no-goods to prune aggressively, which can outperform general-purpose MIP encodings on combinatorial feasibility questions of this kind.

For context, prior work has explored mixed-integer programming and SAT-based formulations for playoff elimination, and major leagues such as MLB and the NBA publish daily magic numbers that, if computed rigorously, require full tiebreaker reasoning. The availability of mature CP toolkits such as Google's OR-Tools CP-SAT and MiniZinc has lowered the engineering cost of deploying such models, and sports scheduling more broadly has become a recurring benchmark for the CP community, with the ITC and related challenges spotlighting league construction problems.

The contribution here appears to be primarily a modeling one: showing that the n-day lookahead clinching question maps cleanly onto CP and that this mapping accommodates rule complexity that flow-based methods cannot. Readers interested in empirical scalability—how the approach behaves on full-season NBA or NFL instances, and how it compares against MIP baselines—should consult the paper directly, as those details determine how practical the method is for production magic-number systems. It is plausible that the CP-SAT style hybrid solvers offer the best of both worlds, but firm conclusions would require the benchmarks reported in the original work.

image.alt: A Constraint Programming Approach for $n$-Day Lookahead Playoff Clinching

entries.title: Strikingness-Aware Evaluation for Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
entries.titleJa: 顕著性を考慮した時系列知識グラフ推論の新評価指標
entries.titleEn: Strikingness-Aware Evaluation for Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は時系列知識グラフ推論において、従来のMRRやHits@kでは捉えきれない「予測の意外性・重要性」を考慮した新しい評価枠組みを提案する。事象の珍しさに応じて重み付けすることで、実用的に価値ある推論モデルの選別を可能にすることを狙う。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning (TKGR) aims at inferring missing (especially future) events from historical data. Current evaluation in TKGR uniforml
entries.bodyJa:
時系列知識グラフ(Temporal Knowledge Graph, TKG)推論は、過去のイベント履歴から未来の関係や事象を予測する技術として、金融・安全保障・サプライチェーン分析などで注目を集めている。本論文は、その評価方法そのものに切り込み、従来指標の盲点を補う「顕著性(strikingness)を考慮した評価」を提案している。

TKG推論の標準的な評価指標であるMRR(平均逆順位)やHits@kは、すべての予測対象を均等に扱う。しかし現実には、頻繁に繰り返される定型的なイベント(例えば定例会議や定期的な貿易取引)を当てるのは比較的容易で、こうした「易しい問題」での高スコアが、モデルの真の推論能力を覆い隠してしまうことがある。著者らは、希少で意外性が高く、かつ社会的・分析的価値の大きいイベントをより重く評価する枠組みを示すことで、この問題に対処しようとしている。

具体的には、イベントの出現頻度や文脈的なパターンから「顕著性スコア」を導出し、それを既存の評価指標に組み込む形と見られる。これにより、単に頻出パターンを学習しただけのモデルと、本当に予測の難しい事象を捉えるモデルとを区別しやすくなる可能性がある。

関連分野として、TKG推論ではRE-NET、CyGNet、xERTE、TLogicといった手法が知られ、ICEWSやGDELTといった国際イベントデータセットがベンチマークに使われてきた。これらのベンチマークでは、繰り返し型イベントが多くを占めるため、長らくスコアのインフレが指摘されてきた経緯がある。レコメンドシステム分野でも「人気バイアス」を補正する評価が議論されており、本研究の問題意識はそれと通底するものと言える。

評価指標は研究コミュニティの進む方向を決定づける。顕著性を意識した評価が広く受け入れられれば、TKG分野のモデル設計は、平均的な精度よりも稀少イベントの予測力を重視する方向にシフトする可能性がある。なお本論文の具体的な実験結果や指標定義の詳細は原文を参照されたい。
entries.bodyEn:
Temporal knowledge graph (TKG) reasoning, which predicts future facts from historical event sequences, has gained traction in domains ranging from geopolitical analysis to financial forecasting and supply chain monitoring. This paper takes aim not at a new model but at how such models are evaluated, proposing a strikingness-aware framework that rewards predictions of rare and meaningful events.

The dominant metrics in TKG reasoning, mean reciprocal rank (MRR) and Hits@k, treat every test query as equally important. In practice, however, much of a TKG's content consists of repetitive, predictable patterns such as recurring diplomatic meetings or routine trade flows. Models that simply memorize these regularities can post impressive scores without demonstrating genuine reasoning ability. The authors argue that this leads to inflated leaderboards and obscures progress on the predictions that actually matter for downstream users.

To address this, the proposed framework appears to assign each event a strikingness weight derived from its frequency and contextual rarity, then folds that weight into standard ranking metrics. The effect is to penalize models that excel only on easy, high-frequency targets while elevating those that handle surprising, low-frequency events well. This reframing could meaningfully change how TKG methods are compared, although the exact formulation and empirical validation are best examined in the paper itself.

The concern resonates with broader trends in machine learning evaluation. Recommender systems research has long grappled with popularity bias, where models that simply surface trending items appear strong on aggregate metrics while failing the long tail. Information retrieval has its own family of utility-weighted metrics such as nDCG with custom gains. In knowledge graph completion more generally, researchers have pointed out that filtered MRR can still reward shortcut learning. A strikingness-aware metric is in that lineage, adapted to the temporal setting where event frequencies vary dramatically over time.

The TKG reasoning literature includes well-known approaches such as RE-NET, CyGNet, xERTE, TLogic, and more recent transformer or diffusion-style models, typically benchmarked on ICEWS subsets and GDELT. Because these datasets are dominated by recurring events, prior analyses have shown that even simple frequency-based baselines can be competitive. A metric that explicitly downweights such easy cases may help expose where genuine progress is being made and where it is not.

If adopted, strikingness-aware evaluation could nudge model design toward architectures that handle novelty and regime change, rather than those tuned for average-case accuracy on repetitive streams. That direction aligns with how TKG reasoning is often pitched to practitioners, namely as a tool for anticipating unusual or consequential developments. Whether the community converges on this specific formulation or on a related variant remains to be seen, but the underlying critique of current benchmarks looks well-founded.

image.alt: Strikingness-Aware Evaluation for Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning

entries.title: Formal Conjectures: An Open and Evolving Benchmark for Verified Discovery in Mathematics
entries.titleJa: Formal Conjectures: 数学発見の検証ベンチマーク
entries.titleEn: Formal Conjectures: An Open and Evolving Benchmark for Verified Discovery in Mathematics
entries.summaryJa: Lean 4で記述された未解決問題・予想群のオープンなベンチマーク「Formal Conjectures」が公開された。AIによる数学的発見を形式的に検証可能にし、進化し続けるリポジトリとして自動定理証明研究を支える狙いがある。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As automated reasoning systems advance rapidly, there is a growing need for research-level formal mathematical problems to accurately evaluate their cap
entries.bodyJa:
AIによる数学的推論能力の評価には、解答が一意に定まる演習問題ではなく、未解決の予想や難題への取り組みを検証する枠組みが求められている。Formal Conjecturesは、その目的に応えるべくLean 4で記述されたオープンかつ進化し続けるベンチマークである。

本ベンチマークは、数学の各分野にまたがる未解決問題や著名な予想を形式言語で記述し、AIシステムが生成した証明や反例をLeanの型システムによって厳密に検証可能にする点に特徴がある。従来のminiF2FやProofNetといったベンチマークは主に教科書レベルの問題や既知の定理を対象としており、フロンティアの数学的発見を評価する用途には限界があった。Formal Conjecturesはこれを補完し、解かれていない命題そのものを扱う姿勢を打ち出している。

リポジトリが「進化し続ける(evolving)」点も重要と見られる。数学コミュニティからの寄稿により問題が追加・洗練され、解決された予想は実績として記録される構造が想定される。この設計は、AIモデルの単発的な性能比較を超え、長期的な発見プロセスそのものを追跡する基盤になり得る。

背景として、近年DeepMindのAlphaProofやAlphaGeometry、Terence Tao氏らによるLeanを使った大規模形式化プロジェクト、Mathlibライブラリの拡大など、機械可読な数学の生態系が急速に整いつつある。LLMと記号的証明支援系を組み合わせたneuro-symbolicアプローチも盛んで、形式化されたターゲットの不足が研究のボトルネックとなっていた。本ベンチマークはその空白を埋める試みと位置付けられる。
entries.bodyEn:
Evaluating AI systems on genuine mathematical reasoning requires more than textbook exercises with known answers. Formal Conjectures, an open and evolving benchmark, addresses this by collecting unsolved problems and famous conjectures formalized in Lean 4, allowing any candidate proof or counterexample to be machine-verified.

The benchmark distinguishes itself from prior efforts such as miniF2F and ProofNet, which largely target competition problems or previously proven theorems. By focusing on open problems across multiple branches of mathematics, Formal Conjectures shifts the evaluation target from rediscovery to genuine discovery. The use of Lean 4 means that any solution produced by an AI system must pass through a rigorous kernel check, eliminating the ambiguity that plagues natural-language proof evaluation.

A key design choice is that the repository is intended to evolve. New conjectures can be contributed, refined, or marked as resolved over time, turning the benchmark into a living record of progress rather than a static leaderboard. This structure could help the community track not only model performance on a fixed set of problems but also the longer arc of automated mathematical discovery.

The project sits within a rapidly maturing ecosystem of machine-readable mathematics. DeepMind's AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry have demonstrated competition-level results using Lean and symbolic search, while large-scale formalization projects led by figures such as Terence Tao and Kevin Buzzard, together with the steadily growing Mathlib library, are putting more of mathematics within reach of automated tools. Neuro-symbolic approaches that combine large language models with interactive theorem provers have shown promise, but progress has been constrained by the limited supply of well-formalized, research-level targets.

Formal Conjectures appears to fill precisely that gap. By providing a curated, verified set of open problems, it offers a meaningful proving ground for next-generation systems that aspire to contribute to mathematics rather than merely imitate it. Whether the benchmark will see widespread adoption likely depends on the breadth of contributions and the ease with which researchers can integrate it into existing Lean-based pipelines, but the direction it points toward is clear.

image.alt: Formal Conjectures: An Open and Evolving Benchmark for Verified Discovery in Mathematics

entries.title: Hierarchical Attacks for Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Reasoning
entries.titleJa: マルチモーダル多エージェント推論への階層的攻撃手法
entries.titleEn: Hierarchical Attacks for Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Reasoning
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はマルチモーダルかつ複数エージェントで構成される推論システムに対する階層的な攻撃手法を提案する。エージェント間の役割や情報伝播の階層構造を悪用し、画像やテキストを介して連鎖的に誤った推論を誘発できることを示す。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-modal multi-agent systems (MM-MAS) have gained increasing attention for their capacity to enable complex reasoning and coordination across diverse
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)を中核に据えたマルチエージェント・システムは、画像・音声・テキストといった複数モダリティを扱う複雑な推論タスクで成果を上げつつある。本論文は、こうしたマルチモーダル多エージェント推論パイプラインに対する「階層的攻撃(Hierarchical Attacks)」を提案し、その脆弱性を体系的に検討している。

提案手法の特徴は、単一エージェント・単一モダリティに閉じた従来の敵対的摂動と異なり、エージェント間の役割分担や情報の階層的な伝播経路を利用する点にある。たとえば、上流エージェントが処理する画像に微小な摂動を加えることで、それを参照する下流エージェントのテキスト推論まで誤らせる連鎖的誤誘導が可能になると見られる。攻撃は階層構造を意識して設計されており、システム全体の意思決定を効率的に歪められる可能性がある。

背景として、近年は AutoGen、LangGraph、CrewAI といったマルチエージェント・フレームワークが普及し、視覚言語モデル(VLM)を介した協調推論の事例も増えている。一方で、プロンプトインジェクションや間接的プロンプト攻撃に関する研究は単一エージェント中心で進められてきた経緯があり、エージェント間の相互作用に着目した安全性評価はまだ限定的である。本研究はその空白を埋める試みと位置づけられる。

また、画像中に埋め込まれた指示文や微小な敵対的パターンがVLMの出力を操作しうることは、既にいくつかの研究で報告されている。多エージェント環境ではこうした攻撃が単に局所的な誤分類にとどまらず、議論・投票・役割分担を経て増幅されるリスクがあるとみられる。実運用では、エージェント間メッセージのサニタイズやモダリティ越境時の検証、信頼度の伝播管理などが対策候補となり得るだろう。

なお、本要約は提示された情報に基づくものであり、実験設定や具体的な防御手法の有効性については原論文を参照する必要がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Multi-agent systems built on top of large language models and vision-language models are increasingly used to tackle complex reasoning tasks that span images, text, and other modalities. This paper introduces a class of hierarchical adversarial attacks aimed specifically at such multi-modal, multi-agent reasoning pipelines, and examines how their layered structure can itself become an attack surface.

Unlike conventional adversarial perturbations that target a single model and a single modality, hierarchical attacks are designed around the role hierarchy and the information flow between agents. A small perturbation introduced into an image consumed by an upstream visual agent, for example, may propagate through intermediate summaries and into the textual reasoning of downstream agents, biasing the collective answer. By explicitly modeling this propagation, the attacker can steer system-level decisions more efficiently than by attacking any individual component in isolation.

The work sits at the intersection of several active research threads. Frameworks such as AutoGen, LangGraph, and CrewAI have made multi-agent orchestration mainstream, and many real deployments now mix VLMs with tool-using text agents. At the same time, the security community has documented prompt injection, indirect injection via retrieved content, and adversarial images that hijack VLM outputs. Most of that prior work, however, focuses on a single agent. Studying how these vulnerabilities compose across roles and modalities is comparatively underexplored, and this paper appears intended to help close that gap.

The hierarchical framing matters because multi-agent setups can both dampen and amplify errors. Debate, voting, and critic-style architectures are sometimes proposed as defenses, since independent agents may catch each other's mistakes. But when a perturbation is crafted with the hierarchy in mind, the same mechanisms can entrench a wrong answer: a confidently mistaken upstream report may be treated as evidence by downstream reasoners, and consensus protocols can lock in the bias. The paper's attacks seem to exploit precisely this dynamic, although the exact extent will depend on the experimental settings reported in the full text.

For practitioners, the implications point toward defense strategies that take the multi-agent topology seriously. Candidate mitigations include sanitizing inter-agent messages, re-validating modality crossings (for instance, recomputing image-derived claims with an independent model), tracking provenance and confidence as information moves through the graph, and stress-testing pipelines with red-team agents that simulate hierarchical adversaries. Standard single-model robustness training is unlikely to be sufficient on its own.

Readers should treat the specifics here as a high-level interpretation; the concrete threat model, datasets, and quantitative results should be consulted in the original paper. Still, the broader message is consistent with a growing consensus in the field: as agentic systems gain autonomy and combine modalities, their security posture must be evaluated at the system level, not just per model.

image.alt: Hierarchical Attacks for Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Reasoning

entries.title: An Agentic AI Framework with Large Language Models and Chain-of-Thought for UAV-Assisted Logistics Scheduling with Mobile Edge Computing
entries.titleJa: LLMと連鎖思考でUAV物流とMECを統合するエージェント型AI枠組み
entries.titleEn: An Agentic AI Framework with Large Language Models and Chain-of-Thought for UAV-Assisted Logistics Scheduling with Mobile Edge Computing
entries.summaryJa: 本研究は、大規模言語モデルと連鎖思考推論を活用したエージェント型AIフレームワークを提案し、モバイルエッジコンピューティングを伴うUAV支援物流のスケジューリング最適化を目指す。配送効率と計算負荷分散の両立が狙いである。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cloud manufacturing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can support both product collection and mobile edge computing (MEC). This joint operation forms
entries.bodyJa:
無人航空機(UAV)を活用した物流配送は、ラストマイル問題への有力な解決策として注目されている。本論文は、大規模言語モデル(LLM)と連鎖思考(Chain-of-Thought, CoT)推論を組み合わせたエージェント型AIフレームワークを提案し、モバイルエッジコンピューティング(MEC)環境下でのUAV物流スケジューリング最適化に取り組んでいる。

従来のUAVスケジューリングは、混合整数計画法や強化学習などの数理的手法に依存してきたが、動的環境への柔軟な対応や、複雑な制約条件下での説明可能な意思決定には課題があった。提案手法では、LLMを推論エンジンとして用い、CoTにより段階的な思考プロセスを経てタスク割当・経路計画・計算オフロードの判断を行うとされる。エージェントが環境状態を観測し、自然言語ベースで方針を導出する点が特徴と見られる。

MECとの統合は、UAV搭載の限られた計算資源を補完する観点で重要である。重い推論処理をエッジサーバーへオフロードしつつ、低遅延通信を維持することで、リアルタイム性が求められる配送判断を支援する設計と考えられる。近年はAmazon Prime Airや中国のMeituanなどが商用UAV配送を進めており、学術界でもエージェント型AIによる物流最適化研究が活発化している。

LLMエージェントを実世界の制御ループに組み込む動きは、AutoGenやLangGraphといったフレームワークの普及とも軌を一にしている。一方で、推論の遅延・コスト・幻覚リスクといった実用上の課題は残されており、本研究のような領域特化型フレームワークが、これらの限界をどこまで克服できるかが今後の焦点となる可能性がある。なお当該プレプリントの詳細な評価指標や実機検証範囲については原文の確認が必要である。
entries.bodyEn:
Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as a compelling solution to the persistent last-mile delivery problem in modern logistics. This paper introduces an agentic AI framework that combines large language models (LLMs) with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to optimize UAV-assisted logistics scheduling in environments augmented by mobile edge computing (MEC).

Traditional approaches to UAV scheduling have relied on mathematical programming, heuristics, or reinforcement learning. While effective in static settings, these methods often struggle to adapt to dynamic conditions and provide limited explainability when handling complex multi-constraint scenarios such as battery limits, weather variability, and time windows. The proposed framework reportedly uses an LLM as a reasoning engine, with CoT prompting that breaks decision-making into intermediate steps covering task allocation, route planning, and computational offloading. By framing the agent's policy in natural language, the system aims to make its choices both flexible and interpretable.

The integration with MEC is significant because UAVs are inherently constrained in onboard compute, energy, and payload. Offloading heavier inference workloads to nearby edge servers, while maintaining low-latency wireless links, can plausibly help sustain real-time decision-making during flight. This mirrors a broader industry trend: Amazon Prime Air, Alphabet's Wing, and China's Meituan have all advanced commercial drone delivery, and academic research on agentic optimization for logistics has accelerated in parallel.

The rise of LLM-based agents in operational control loops also dovetails with the maturation of orchestration frameworks such as AutoGen, LangGraph, and CrewAI, which make multi-step tool use and planning more tractable. However, deploying LLM agents in safety-sensitive, latency-critical domains like aerial logistics raises legitimate concerns. Inference latency, token cost, and hallucination risk remain non-trivial obstacles, and verifying that a language-model-driven planner respects hard physical and regulatory constraints is an open research question.

Domain-specialized frameworks like the one described in this paper may help narrow that gap by constraining the agent's reasoning space and grounding outputs in verified state information from the MEC layer. Whether such designs can outperform well-tuned classical optimizers under realistic workloads, or whether they primarily add value through adaptability and explainability, will likely depend on empirical evaluation. Readers interested in the precise benchmarks, baselines, and simulation or hardware-in-the-loop setups used here should consult the preprint directly, as the abstract-level description leaves room for interpretation regarding the maturity of the approach.

Overall, the work sits at the intersection of three rapidly evolving fields: agentic AI, edge computing, and autonomous aerial systems. Even if the immediate contributions are incremental, the conceptual direction of using LLM reasoning to coordinate fleets of UAVs with edge infrastructure appears to be gaining momentum, and could inform future standards for intelligent logistics orchestration.

image.alt: An Agentic AI Framework with Large Language Models and Chain-of-Thought for UAV-Assisted Logistics Scheduling with Mobile Edge Computing

entries.title: Improving Code Translation with Syntax-Guided and Semantic-aware Preference Optimization
entries.titleJa: 構文誘導と意味理解に基づく選好最適化によるコード翻訳の改善
entries.titleEn: Improving Code Translation with Syntax-Guided and Semantic-aware Preference Optimization
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、LLMを用いたコード間翻訳の精度向上を目的に、構文ガイドと意味認識に基づく選好最適化(SSPO)手法を提案する。構文・意味の両面から翻訳の良し悪しを評価し、DPO的な学習で誤りを抑制することで、従来手法より高い実行成功率を達成したと報告している。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs have shown immense potential for code translation, yet they often struggle to ensure both syntactic correctness and semantic consistency. While pre
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)を用いたプログラミング言語間のコード翻訳は、レガシー資産の近代化やマルチ言語開発の効率化に直結する応用として注目を集めている。一方で、生成されたコードは表面的には妥当に見えても、コンパイルが通らない、あるいは入力に対し期待と異なる挙動を示すといった欠陥がしばしば発生する。本論文はこの課題に対し、構文ガイドかつ意味認識型の選好最適化(Syntax-guided and Semantic-aware Preference Optimization, 通称SSPO)を提案するものと見られる。

手法の骨子は、複数の翻訳候補を生成したうえで、構文的な健全性(パース可能か、型整合が取れるか等)と、意味的な等価性(テスト実行による振る舞いの一致)の双方を評価軸として候補をランク付けし、優劣ペアを用いてDPO(Direct Preference Optimization)系の選好学習を行う点にあると考えられる。単純な教師あり微調整(SFT)では正解コードを模倣するに留まり、構文崩壊や微妙な意味のズレを十分に抑えられないが、選好最適化では「より悪い候補」を明示的に避けるよう学習が進むため、実行成功率(CA, Computational Accuracy)で優位が出やすい。

背景として、コード翻訳ベンチマークにはCodeNetやTransCoder、AVATARなどがあり、Java/Python/C++間の相互翻訳が標準的に評価されている。OpenAIのCodexやMetaのTransCoder、近年のCode Llama、DeepSeek-Coder、Qwen-Coderなど、コード特化LLMが続々と登場するなかで、単純な規模拡大ではなく学習信号の質を高めるアプローチが重要性を増している。SSPOのように実行結果や静的解析を報酬信号に取り込む流れは、RLHFやRLAIFのコード版とも位置付けられ、AlphaCodeやリフレクション系手法とも親和性が高い可能性がある。

実務的には、業務システムのCOBOLからJavaへの移行や、機械学習コードのPyTorch/JAX相互変換など、テストケースが整備できるドメインで効果が出やすいと推測される。一方、テストが乏しい領域では意味報酬の設計が課題となり、静的解析や形式的検証との組み合わせが今後の論点となるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
Translating source code between programming languages with large language models has become a practical lever for legacy modernization and polyglot development. Yet LLM-generated translations frequently look plausible on the surface while failing to compile or producing subtly different runtime behavior. This paper proposes a Syntax-guided and Semantic-aware Preference Optimization approach, abbreviated SSPO, that targets exactly these two failure modes during fine-tuning.

The core idea, as far as can be inferred from the title and abstract framing, is to move beyond standard supervised fine-tuning, where a model merely imitates reference translations. Instead, the system samples multiple candidate translations for each source program and scores them along two axes: syntactic validity, judged by whether the output parses, type-checks, or otherwise conforms to language rules, and semantic equivalence, judged by executing the candidate against test cases and comparing observable behavior to the original. The resulting preference pairs feed a DPO-style objective so the model learns not only what good translations look like but also which kinds of mistakes to actively avoid.

This matters because computational accuracy, the rate at which translated code actually passes the original test suite, has historically lagged token-level metrics like BLEU or CodeBLEU. Supervised fine-tuning rewards surface similarity, so a model can be punished for a semantically correct but stylistically different rendering, while a near-miss that silently breaks an edge case may be reinforced. Preference optimization with execution-grounded signals reverses that incentive structure, which is plausibly why SSPO is reported to outperform baseline tuning recipes on standard benchmarks.

The broader context is a crowded research line. TransCoder from Meta pioneered unsupervised code translation, CodeNet and AVATAR provide cross-lingual parallel corpora, and code-specialized LLMs such as Code Llama, DeepSeek-Coder, Qwen-Coder, and StarCoder2 have raised the floor on raw generation quality. Recent work increasingly treats execution as a first-class training signal, echoing RLHF and RLAIF developments in general-purpose chat models, and connecting to self-debugging or reflection pipelines like Self-Refine and AlphaCodium. SSPO can be read as a focused instance of this trend, narrowing the reward to two well-defined and cheaply computable signals rather than a vague human preference.

For practitioners, the approach seems most immediately useful where a credible test suite exists, for example migrating numerical or algorithmic code between Python, Java, and C++, or porting machine learning kernels between PyTorch and JAX. In such settings, execution-based preference data can be generated at scale with minimal human effort. The harder open question, not fully resolved by this paper as far as can be told, is how to extend the recipe to domains with sparse tests, large framework dependencies, or side-effect-heavy code such as web backends and systems software. Here, complementary signals from static analyzers, type inference, or even lightweight formal verification may be needed, and combining SSPO with property-based test generation looks like a natural next step.

Overall, the contribution appears incremental but well-targeted: it does not propose a new base model, but it sharpens the training signal in a way that directly attacks the dominant failure modes of LLM code translation. If the reported gains hold across languages and model sizes, similar preference-shaping techniques are likely to be absorbed quickly into open-source code model recipes.

image.alt: Improving Code Translation with Syntax-Guided and Semantic-aware Preference Optimization

entries.title: It's not the Language Model, it's the Tool: Deterministic Mediation for Scientific Workflows
entries.titleJa: 言語モデルではなくツールの問題:科学ワークフローの決定論的仲介
entries.titleEn: It's not the Language Model, it's the Tool: Deterministic Mediation for Scientific Workflows
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、LLMを用いた科学ワークフローの信頼性問題は、モデル自体ではなくツール側の設計に起因すると主張する。決定論的な仲介層を介してツール呼び出しを制御することで、再現性と正確性を高めるアプローチを提案している。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models can produce convincing scientific analyses, but repeated generations on the same data do not guarantee the same result. A researcher may
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)を科学研究の自動化に活用する動きが広がる中、本論文は信頼性の根本的な原因はモデルではなくツール側にあるという視点を提示している。著者らは、LLMが科学ワークフローで誤った結果を生む主因を、確率的なモデル出力そのものではなく、ツールの曖昧な仕様や非決定的な振る舞いに求めている。

論文の中心的な主張は、ツール呼び出しを決定論的に仲介する層を導入することで、LLMの確率的性質を保ちつつワークフロー全体の再現性を担保できるというものだ。具体的には、ツールの入出力スキーマを厳密化し、副作用を制御可能な形に整理することで、エージェントが同じ条件下で同じ結果を返せるようにする設計が示されているとみられる。

背景として、近年は LangChain、LlamaIndex、OpenAI の Function Calling、Anthropic の Model Context Protocol(MCP)など、LLMと外部ツールを接続する枠組みが急速に整備されている。一方で、科学計算や実験記録のように厳密な再現性が要求される領域では、LLMエージェントの「うっかり」が研究の妥当性を損なう懸念が指摘されてきた。本研究はこの溝を埋める試みと位置付けられる。

また、決定論的仲介という考え方は、データベース分野におけるトランザクション制御や、ワークフローエンジン(Airflow、Nextflow、Snakemake など)における冪等性の議論とも親和性が高い。LLMエージェントを「賢いオーケストレーター」として扱うのではなく、決定論的基盤の上で動く「探索的フロントエンド」とみなす設計思想への移行を示唆している可能性がある。今後、科学分野以外でも同様の議論が広がるか注目される。
entries.bodyEn:
As large language models increasingly drive automated scientific workflows, this paper makes a pointed argument: the reliability problems we attribute to LLMs often originate not in the model itself, but in the tools the model is asked to call. The authors reframe the debate around agentic science by shifting attention from probabilistic generation to the deterministic substrate that should support it.

The central claim is that scientific workflows fail reproducibly not because LLMs hallucinate, but because the tools they invoke have ambiguous specifications, uncontrolled side effects, or non-deterministic behavior. When an agent calls a poorly specified function, even a perfectly behaved model can produce divergent outcomes across runs. The proposed remedy is a deterministic mediation layer that sits between the language model and the underlying tools, enforcing strict input and output schemas, controlling side effects, and ensuring that identical invocations yield identical results.

This framing is timely. The past two years have seen rapid growth in tool-calling frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI function calling, and more recently Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP). These ecosystems make it easy to expose arbitrary capabilities to an LLM, but they generally do not impose the kind of determinism that scientific reproducibility demands. In domains like computational biology, chemistry, or physics, where a single misordered parameter can invalidate downstream conclusions, this gap is more than a developer convenience issue.

The authors' approach echoes long-standing ideas from adjacent fields. Workflow engines like Airflow, Nextflow, and Snakemake have for years emphasized idempotency, content-addressed caching, and explicit data lineage. Database systems have similarly relied on strict transactional semantics to make probabilistic workloads tractable. Viewed in that light, the paper can be read as advocating that LLM agents be treated less as autonomous orchestrators and more as exploratory front-ends that sit atop a deterministic execution core. The intelligence remains stochastic; the substrate does not.

There are several practical implications worth noting. First, tool authors may need to invest more effort in formal interface design, including typed schemas, versioning, and explicit declarations of side effects. Second, evaluation of agent systems may need to disentangle model error from tool error, since current benchmarks often conflate the two. Third, the approach could make it easier to audit scientific results produced with LLM assistance, an increasingly important consideration as journals and funders begin to scrutinize AI-assisted research.

The argument is not that language models are blameless. Rather, it suggests that improving tool design may yield larger reliability gains, at lower cost, than continued scaling of the model alone. Whether this perspective gains broader traction will likely depend on how the emerging MCP-style ecosystems evolve, and whether tool vendors adopt the kind of deterministic discipline the authors advocate. It is plausible that similar arguments will surface in non-scientific domains, such as financial analysis or legal workflows, where reproducibility carries comparable weight.

image.alt: It's not the Language Model, it's the Tool: Deterministic Mediation for Scientific Workflows

entries.title: Respecting Self-Uncertainty in On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient LLM Reasoning
entries.titleJa: 自己不確実性を尊重するオンポリシー自己蒸留によるLLM推論の効率化
entries.titleEn: Respecting Self-Uncertainty in On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient LLM Reasoning
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、大規模言語モデルの推論能力を効率的に強化するため、モデル自身の不確実性を考慮したオンポリシー自己蒸留手法を提案する。教師信号を一律に押し付けず、学習者の確信度に応じて蒸留強度を調整することで、推論タスクの精度と学習効率を両立させる狙いがある。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy self-distillation trains a reasoning model on its own rollouts while a teacher, often the same model conditioned on privileged context, provid
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)の推論能力を強化する手法として、知識蒸留や強化学習が広く用いられているが、計算コストと学習の安定性の両立は依然として課題である。本論文は、モデル自身が抱える「自己不確実性」を尊重しながら、オンポリシーでの自己蒸留を行う新たな枠組みを提案する。

従来の蒸留では、教師モデルが生成した分布や応答を一律に模倣させる傾向があり、学習者がすでに高い確信を持って正解できるサンプルにも過剰な信号を与え、逆にモデル本来の挙動を歪める恐れがあった。提案手法では、生徒モデルが自ら生成した軌跡(オンポリシー)に基づき、出力分布のエントロピーや確信度を測定し、蒸留損失の重み付けを動的に調整する。これにより、不確実な箇所に集中的に学習資源を割り当てる設計と見られる。

推論タスク、特に数学や論理推論のように多段階の思考連鎖を要する問題では、誤った中間ステップが連鎖的に最終解答を狂わせる。自己生成ロールアウトに対する選択的な蒸留は、こうしたエラー伝播を抑制し、サンプル効率を改善する可能性がある。

関連動向として、DeepSeek-R1やOpenAIのo1系モデルが示したように、推論特化型LLMでは強化学習や蒸留の組み合わせが重要なレシピとなっている。また、自己蒸留(self-distillation)はラベル平滑化に類似した正則化効果を持つことが知られており、最近ではon-policy RLHFやDPO系手法との融合も研究が進む。本手法は、教師モデルに依存しない自己改善ループの一形態として、計算リソースが限られる環境でも有効な選択肢となり得る。

なお、提示されたURLからは詳細な実験結果や比較対象を確認できなかったため、性能の優位性については論文本体を参照する必要がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) typically relies on knowledge distillation or reinforcement learning, but balancing compute cost with training stability remains an open problem. This paper introduces an on-policy self-distillation framework that explicitly respects the model's own uncertainty when shaping the learning signal.

Conventional distillation tends to force a student to mimic teacher distributions uniformly, regardless of whether the student already handles a given example with high confidence. This can waste capacity and even distort behaviors the student has correctly internalized. The proposed method instead measures the student's predictive entropy or confidence on its own rollouts and modulates the distillation loss accordingly. In effect, the training signal concentrates on regions where the student is genuinely uncertain, while leaving confident, correct behaviors largely untouched.

This design appears particularly well suited to multi-step reasoning tasks such as mathematics or logical inference, where a single erroneous intermediate step can derail an entire chain of thought. By distilling selectively on self-generated trajectories, the approach may suppress error propagation and improve sample efficiency compared to off-policy or uniformly weighted distillation. Operating on-policy also keeps the training distribution aligned with the model's deployment behavior, which is generally considered beneficial for stability.

The work fits into a broader trend in reasoning-focused LLMs. Systems such as DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI's o1 family have highlighted how combinations of reinforcement learning, rejection sampling, and distillation can unlock substantial reasoning gains. Self-distillation itself has long been studied as a form of implicit regularization, sometimes likened to label smoothing, and recent literature has begun blending it with on-policy reinforcement learning and preference optimization methods like DPO. The notion of uncertainty-aware weighting also echoes ideas from active learning and curriculum learning, where the most informative examples drive the bulk of progress.

A notable practical advantage is that self-distillation removes the dependence on a stronger external teacher, which can be costly or unavailable for frontier-scale models. Teams operating under limited compute budgets, or working with proprietary models that cannot easily be queried as teachers, may find this style of self-improvement loop attractive. That said, self-distillation methods can plateau or even degrade if the model reinforces its own biases, so the uncertainty-gated formulation may serve as a useful safeguard against such collapse, though this should be validated empirically.

Because the linked source did not expose full experimental details in this review, claims about absolute performance gains, scaling behavior, and comparisons to standard RLHF or rejection-sampling fine-tuning should be checked against the paper itself. Still, the conceptual contribution, treating the learner's own uncertainty as a first-class signal in self-distillation, aligns with a growing consensus that smarter use of training signal, rather than simply more data or larger teachers, is a key lever for efficient reasoning in LLMs.

image.alt: Respecting Self-Uncertainty in On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient LLM Reasoning

entries.title: Differentiable Learning of Lifted Action Schemas for Classical Planning
entries.titleJa: 古典プランニング向けリフト型行動スキーマの微分可能学習
entries.titleEn: Differentiable Learning of Lifted Action Schemas for Classical Planning
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、古典プランニング問題における行動スキーマ(変数化された行動定義)を微分可能な枠組みで学習する手法を提案する。観測された計画軌跡から、PDDLに類するリフト表現を勾配法で獲得し、未知ドメインへの汎化と記号的推論の両立を狙う。
