entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical planners can effectively solve very large deterministic MDPs represented in STRIPS or PDDL where states are sets of atoms over objects and rel
entries.bodyJa:
古典プランニングにおいて、行動の前提条件と効果を変数化して記述した「リフト型行動スキーマ」は、PDDLに代表される標準的な知識表現である。本論文は、このスキーマを人手で書く代わりに、観測データから微分可能な最適化によって自動学習する枠組みを提示している。

従来、行動モデル学習(action model learning)は ARMS や LOCM のような記号的・組合せ的手法が中心で、ノイズや部分観測への耐性、スケーラビリティに課題があった。一方、深層学習ベースの方策学習は汎化に強みを持つが、得られたモデルは不透明で、リフト表現が持つ「オブジェクト数に依存しない汎化」を失いがちである。本研究はその中間を狙い、スキーマのパラメータ(述語と引数の割り当て)を連続緩和し、勾配法で最適化する設計と見られる。

具体的には、計画軌跡(状態と行動の系列)を入力に、各行動スキーマの前提条件・追加効果・削除効果を表す述語の選択を確率的に表現し、軌跡の整合性を最大化するように学習する構成が想定される。学習後はしきい値処理などで離散的なPDDL風スキーマに変換でき、既存のプランナで利用可能になる点が実用上の利点となる。

関連動向としては、Neuro-Symbolic AI の流れの中で、LatPlan による画像からの潜在記号獲得、あるいは大規模言語モデルを用いたPDDL生成の試みなど、記号的プランニングと学習の橋渡しが活発化している。リフト表現を直接学習するアプローチは、グラウンディングを介する手法に比べてオブジェクト数のスケーリングに有利と考えられ、ロボティクスやゲームAIへの応用余地がある。

一方で、述語語彙そのものの発見や、関数的・数値的効果への拡張、ノイズの多い実環境データへの頑健性などは依然として課題と見られる。なお、arXiv ID の年次表記には注意が必要で、引用時には原著の発表年・会議を確認することが望ましい。
entries.bodyEn:
Lifted action schemas, the variable-parameterised operator definitions familiar from PDDL, are the standard way classical planning encodes how the world changes. This paper proposes learning such schemas directly from data via a differentiable optimisation framework, rather than relying on hand-authored domain models.

Traditional action model learning has been dominated by symbolic and combinatorial systems such as ARMS, LOCM and SAM, which extract preconditions and effects from plan traces using logical constraints. These methods are precise when data is clean but tend to struggle with noise, partial observability and scale. Conversely, deep learning approaches to policy or world-model learning generalise well empirically but yield opaque representations that lose the object-count-invariant generalisation that lifted symbolic representations provide almost for free.

The contribution sits between these traditions. The authors appear to represent the choice of predicates and argument bindings for each schema's preconditions, add-effects and delete-effects as continuous, differentiable parameters. Training maximises consistency with observed state-action trajectories, and after convergence the soft parameters can be discretised, via thresholding or argmax, into a PDDL-compatible operator set. The practical payoff is that the resulting domain can be fed into any off-the-shelf classical planner such as Fast Downward, combining gradient-based learning with sound symbolic search at deployment time.

This line of work fits within the broader neuro-symbolic agenda. LatPlan demonstrated learning latent propositional symbols from images, while more recent efforts use large language models to draft or repair PDDL domains from natural-language descriptions. Compared with grounded approaches that enumerate all object instantiations, learning at the lifted level should scale more gracefully with object count, which matters for robotics manipulation domains and procedurally generated game environments where the number of entities varies at test time.

Several caveats are worth flagging. Differentiable schema induction typically assumes a known predicate vocabulary; discovering the predicates themselves remains harder and is often handled by separate representation-learning stages. Extensions to numeric fluents, conditional effects, durative actions and probabilistic outcomes are non-trivial, and robustness to noisy or partially observed trajectories from real sensors is an open question. The expressive gap between what gradient descent can recover and what richer fragments of PDDL allow is likely to be a continuing research theme.

Readers should also note that arXiv identifiers occasionally appear with unusual year prefixes in metadata; verifying the canonical venue and publication year of the underlying work is advisable before citing. Overall, if the approach delivers on its premise, it offers a pragmatic route to bootstrapping planning domains in settings where writing PDDL by hand is the bottleneck, while keeping the interpretability and combinatorial leverage that makes classical planning attractive in the first place.

entries.title: What properties of reasoning supervision are associated with improved downstream model quality?
entries.titleJa: 推論監督のどの特性が下流モデル品質向上に寄与するか
entries.titleEn: What properties of reasoning supervision are associated with improved downstream model quality?
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、思考連鎖(CoT)などの推論監督データが持つどの特性が、ファインチューニング後のモデル品質を高めるかを分析。長さ・多様性・正確性といった要素を切り分けて比較し、効果的な推論教師データの設計指針を探る。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Validating training data for reasoning models typically requires expensive trial-and-error fine-tuning cycles. In this work, we investigate whether the
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデルの推論能力を高める手段として、思考連鎖(Chain-of-Thought, CoT)を含む推論監督データによるファインチューニングが急速に普及している。本研究は、その「どんな推論データが効くのか」という根本的な問いに踏み込み、教師データの性質と下流タスク性能の関係を体系的に分析するものである。

論文では、推論監督データを構成する複数の要因——推論ステップの長さ、形式の多様性、最終回答の正確性、誤りや回り道の有無、ドメインの広がりなど——を切り分け、それぞれが微調整後のモデル品質に与える影響を比較していると見られる。単純に「長いCoTほど良い」「正解だけを使えばよい」とする直感が、必ずしも当てはまらないケースを示唆している可能性がある。

背景として、DeepSeek-R1やOpenAI o1系列の登場以降、推論トレース自体を学習信号として用いるアプローチが主流化している。蒸留用に大規模な推論データセットを公開する動きも活発で、Open-R1やS1のように「少量だが質の高い推論データ」で高性能を出す事例も注目を集めてきた。本論文の知見は、こうしたデータキュレーション戦略に直接的な示唆を与えると期待される。

また、強化学習(RLVR)による推論能力獲得との比較も論点になりうる。教師あり微調整(SFT)で再現できる推論能力の範囲と、RLによってのみ獲得可能なスキルの境界線を理解する上でも、監督データの特性分析は重要な前提となる。

読者としては、推論データの「量より質」を裏付ける定量的根拠が得られるか、また誤った推論軌跡をあえて含めることが汎化に寄与するかといった、実務的なデータ設計の指針を得られる点に注目したい。なおarXiv IDの形式上、最終版での結論や実験規模は今後の確認が必要である。
entries.bodyEn:
Fine-tuning large language models on reasoning supervision—chain-of-thought traces and longer deliberative outputs—has become a dominant recipe for boosting reasoning ability. This paper tackles a more fundamental question that practitioners face when curating such data: which properties of the reasoning supervision actually correlate with better downstream model quality?

The authors appear to decompose reasoning training data into measurable dimensions such as trace length, stylistic and structural diversity, correctness of the final answer, presence of dead ends or self-corrections, and domain coverage. By varying these factors systematically and observing the resulting fine-tuned model performance, the work aims to separate signal from noise in what is often a fuzzy design space. The framing suggests that intuitive heuristics—longer is better, only correct traces matter, more diversity always helps—may not hold uniformly across settings.

The context for this investigation is the explosion of reasoning-focused training corpora following DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI's o1 family, and the wave of open distillation efforts such as Open-R1, S1, and various LIMA-style minimalist datasets. Recent findings in that ecosystem have repeatedly shown that small but carefully chosen sets of reasoning traces can rival much larger corpora, hinting that supervision quality, not volume, is the binding constraint. A principled study of which qualitative attributes drive this gap is therefore timely and could directly inform data curation pipelines.

Another backdrop is the ongoing debate between supervised fine-tuning on reasoning traces and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Understanding what SFT can and cannot teach—as a function of the supervision's structure—helps delineate where RL-style exploration is necessary and where imitation suffices. If, for instance, traces containing genuine mistakes and recoveries generalize better than polished ones, that would echo emerging results that exposing models to error-correction patterns improves robustness.

For practitioners, the most actionable takeaways are likely to concern filtering policies: whether to keep only verified-correct traces, how aggressively to deduplicate by style, and how much to balance domains. The paper may also bear on synthetic data generation, since teacher models can be prompted to produce traces with specific characteristics once we know which characteristics matter. Teams building reasoning models on a budget could use such guidance to prioritize annotation effort.

Readers should treat specific numerical claims with appropriate caution until the camera-ready version and experimental scope are confirmed, as the abstract-level framing leaves room for interpretation about scale and model families covered. Still, the direction—turning reasoning-data curation from folklore into measurable engineering—aligns with where the field seems to be heading, and complementary work on data attribution and influence functions could eventually make these properties predictive rather than merely correlative. Expect follow-up studies to test whether the identified properties transfer across base model sizes and across reasoning domains such as math, code, and agentic tool use.

entries.title: Discrete Diffusion for Complex and Congested Multi-Agent Path Finding with Sparse Social Attention
entries.titleJa: 離散拡散とスパース社会的注意による複雑・混雑環境下のマルチエージェント経路計画
entries.titleEn: Discrete Diffusion for Complex and Congested Multi-Agent Path Finding with Sparse Social Attention
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、複雑で混雑したマルチエージェント経路探索（MAPF）問題に対し、離散拡散モデルとスパースな社会的注意機構を組み合わせた新手法を提案する。エージェント間の相互作用を効率的に捉え、従来手法より高い解決率とスケーラビリティを実現すると見られる。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) is a coordination problem that requires computing globally consistent, collision-free trajectories from individual start
entries.bodyJa:
マルチエージェント経路探索（MAPF）は、複数のロボットや車両が衝突せずに目的地へ到達する経路を計算する古典的かつ実用的な問題である。倉庫物流、自動運転車群、ゲームAIなどで需要が高まる一方、エージェント数の増加と環境の混雑度に応じて計算量が急速に膨らむという課題を抱えてきた。

本論文は、離散拡散モデル（discrete diffusion）とスパースな社会的注意機構（sparse social attention）を組み合わせた学習ベースのアプローチを提案している。離散拡散は近年、テキスト生成や離散構造データのモデリングで注目を集めている生成手法で、ノイズを段階的に除去しながら離散的な出力（ここでは各エージェントの行動列）を生成する。著者らはこの枠組みを経路計画に応用し、エージェント全体の行動を同時に生成することで、逐次的探索手法が陥りやすいデッドロックや局所最適を回避できる可能性があると見られる。

スパース社会的注意は、近接するエージェント間のみに注意計算を限定することで、全エージェントペアを考慮する密な注意機構の計算量問題を緩和する設計である。混雑シナリオでは隣接関係が動的に変化するため、スパース構造の動的構築が鍵となる。

関連分野では、Conflict-Based Search（CBS）などの探索ベース手法や、PRIMALに代表される強化学習ベースのMAPF手法が広く研究されている。近年は拡散モデルをロボット計画に適用するDiffuserやDecision Diffuserといった研究も登場しており、本論文はその流れを離散領域・マルチエージェント設定に拡張する位置付けと理解できる。実用面では、Amazon Roboticsなどの倉庫運用や自動運転フリート制御に直結するテーマであり、混雑時のスループット改善は産業的価値が高い。なお詳細な実験結果や既存手法に対する優位性の程度はプレプリント本文の確認が必要である。
entries.bodyEn:
Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) is the classical problem of computing collision-free paths for many agents moving toward individual goals. It underpins applications ranging from warehouse robotics and autonomous vehicle fleets to multiplayer game AI. As the number of agents grows and environments become more congested, the combinatorial complexity of MAPF explodes, making scalable and reliable solvers a persistent research challenge.

This paper introduces a learning-based approach that combines discrete diffusion modeling with a sparse social attention mechanism. Discrete diffusion has gained traction recently as a generative framework for categorical data, including text and structured sequences, in which a model learns to iteratively denoise corrupted discrete tokens. The authors apparently adapt this paradigm to MAPF by treating joint agent actions or path tokens as the discrete variables to be generated. By denoising the entire multi-agent plan in parallel, the method may sidestep the sequential bottlenecks and deadlocks that plague traditional search-based or autoregressive learned planners.

The sparse social attention component addresses a well-known scaling issue: dense pairwise attention across all agents quickly becomes intractable in crowded scenarios. By restricting attention to spatially or topologically nearby agents, the model can capture the most relevant interactions while keeping compute bounded. In congested settings, where neighbor relations shift rapidly, the dynamic construction of this sparsity pattern is likely a critical design element.

The broader MAPF literature spans exact search methods like Conflict-Based Search (CBS) and its many variants, prioritized planning, and reinforcement learning approaches such as PRIMAL. More recently, diffusion-based planners like Diffuser and Decision Diffuser have shown that generative models can produce coherent long-horizon trajectories for single-agent control. This work can be read as extending that trajectory-generation lineage into the discrete, combinatorial, multi-agent regime, which is arguably one of the harder testbeds for generative planning.

From an applied perspective, the relevance is clear. Companies operating dense robot fleets, such as Amazon Robotics or autonomous mobile robot vendors in logistics, routinely face throughput limits driven by congestion at intersections and pickup points. Methods that scale gracefully and avoid gridlock under heavy load have direct economic value. Academic benchmarks like the MAPF benchmark suite have also pushed researchers to evaluate on increasingly cluttered grids where classical solvers struggle to find solutions within reasonable time budgets.

Readers should note that, as a preprint, the specific empirical claims, baselines, and the magnitude of improvements warrant direct inspection of the paper. It also remains to be seen how the approach generalizes across map topologies and agent densities not encountered during training, a common concern for learned MAPF solvers. Still, the combination of discrete diffusion and sparse interaction modeling represents a plausible and timely direction, aligning with broader trends in applying modern generative architectures to combinatorial planning problems.

entries.title: Achieving Gold-Medal-Level Olympiad Reasoning via Simple and Unified Scaling
entries.titleJa: シンプルで統一的なスケーリングによる五輪レベルの金メダル推論の達成
entries.titleEn: Achieving Gold-Medal-Level Olympiad Reasoning via Simple and Unified Scaling
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、複雑な強化学習や専用パイプラインに頼らず、シンプルで統一的なスケーリング手法によって、数学オリンピックレベルの推論性能を達成したと報告している。金メダル相当の成績を示し、推論モデル設計に新たな視点を提供する可能性がある。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent progress in reasoning models has substantially advanced long-horizon mathematical and scientific problem solving, with several systems now reachi
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)の推論能力を国際数学オリンピック(IMO)級の水準まで引き上げる試みが各所で進んでいるなか、本論文はシンプルかつ統一的なスケーリングだけで金メダル相当の成績に到達したと報告している。

近年、OpenAI の o1 / o3 系や DeepSeek-R1、Google DeepMind の AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry など、推論特化モデルが相次いで登場し、数学オリンピックは LLM の到達点を測るベンチマークの一つになっている。これらの多くは強化学習(RLHF や RLVR)、専用の検証器、ツール利用、長い chain-of-thought などを組み合わせる複雑な設計を採用してきた。

本論文の主張は、そうした複雑なパイプラインに依存せず、学習・推論時のスケーリングを統一的に行うシンプルな枠組みでも、オリンピックレベルの問題で金メダル相当のスコアが得られるというものだ。具体的なアルゴリズム詳細はアブストラクトレベルでは限定的だが、データ規模・モデル規模・推論時の計算量を一貫した設計思想で拡張することが鍵と見られる。

関連する文脈として、2024 年に DeepMind が IMO で銀メダル相当のスコアを示し、2025 年には OpenAI と Google が相次いで金メダル水準の到達を報告した経緯がある。これらは公式採点ではなく非公式評価である点に注意が必要だが、推論モデル競争は急速に進展している。本研究のように「シンプルさ」を強調するアプローチは、Chinchilla 則以降のスケーリング研究の流れに連なるものと言える。

なお、本記事で参照している arXiv ID は通常の付番形式と異なる可能性があり、内容の最終的な検証には原著へのアクセスが必要である。手法の再現性や評価プロトコルの厳密さは、今後のコミュニティによる検証を待つ必要があるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
Pushing large language models toward International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) level reasoning has become one of the defining benchmarks of frontier AI research. This paper reports that a simple and unified scaling recipe is sufficient to reach gold-medal-level performance on olympiad-style mathematics, challenging the assumption that elaborate training pipelines are required.

Over the past two years, reasoning-specialized systems such as OpenAI's o1 and o3 families, DeepSeek-R1, and Google DeepMind's AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry have dominated the conversation around mathematical reasoning. Most of these systems rely on intricate combinations of reinforcement learning (RLHF or RLVR with verifiable rewards), specialized verifiers, tool use, formal proof assistants like Lean, and very long chain-of-thought traces. The engineering complexity has grown substantially, and reproducing such results outside well-resourced labs has become difficult.

Against that backdrop, the authors argue that a unified scaling strategy, applied consistently across data, model size, and inference-time compute, is enough to attain gold-medal-level scores. While the abstract-level description leaves the precise algorithmic details somewhat opaque, the central claim is methodological parsimony: rather than stacking bespoke components, scale the same simple recipe further. If the result holds up under scrutiny, it would echo earlier scaling-law arguments dating back to the Kaplan and Chinchilla papers, which suggested that capability often emerges from disciplined scaling rather than architectural novelty.

Context matters when interpreting gold-medal claims. In 2024, DeepMind reported silver-medal-equivalent performance at the IMO with AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2. In 2025, both OpenAI and Google announced systems that they claimed reached gold-medal thresholds, though these evaluations were unofficial and the grading protocols varied. Olympiad performance is sensitive to problem selection, time limits, and whether tools or formal verifiers are allowed, so headline scores should be read with care.

There are also reasons for measured skepticism here. The arXiv identifier referenced for this submission does not follow the standard recent numbering pattern, which means readers should verify the original source before drawing firm conclusions. Even setting that aside, claims of simplicity in frontier reasoning research often depend heavily on implicit assumptions, such as the quality of pretraining data, the availability of curated math corpora, or the compute budget allocated to inference-time search. Independent replication, transparent evaluation protocols, and clarity about whether natural-language or formal proofs are produced will determine how influential this work becomes.

If the paper's thesis survives community validation, it could shift attention back toward clean scaling studies and away from increasingly baroque RL pipelines. Practitioners building reasoning systems may find value in revisiting whether their stack's complexity is genuinely contributing to performance, or whether a simpler, more uniformly scaled baseline would suffice. Either way, the trajectory of olympiad-level reasoning benchmarks suggests that what was considered a distant frontier only two years ago is now a routine target for frontier labs.

entries.title: IdeaForge: A Knowledge Graph-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Cross-Methodology Innovation Analysis and Patent Claim Generation
entries.titleJa: IdeaForge: 知識グラフを基盤としたマルチエージェントによる特許請求項生成フレームワーク
entries.titleEn: IdeaForge: A Knowledge Graph-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Cross-Methodology Innovation Analysis and Patent Claim Generation
entries.summaryJa: IdeaForgeは知識グラフを基盤に複数のLLMエージェントを協調させ、異分野の手法を横断したイノベーション分析と特許請求項の自動生成を行う研究フレームワークである。発明アイデアの構造化と請求項記述の精度向上を狙う。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current AI-assisted innovation systems typically apply a single ideation methodology (such as TRIZ or Design Thinking) using sequential prompt-based wor
entries.bodyJa:
特許出願における請求項(claims)の作成は、発明の本質を法的に過不足なく記述する高度な作業であり、AI支援への期待が高まっている。IdeaForgeは、知識グラフを土台に複数のLLMエージェントを協調させ、異分野の手法を横断したイノベーション分析と特許請求項の自動生成を行うフレームワークとして提案されている。

基本的な発想は、単一のLLMにプロンプトで丸投げするのではなく、発明のコンセプト・先行技術・技術領域間の関係を知識グラフとして明示的に構造化し、それを参照しながら役割の異なるエージェント(調査、分析、起草、検証など)が分担して処理する点にあると見られる。知識グラフを共有メモリとして用いることで、複数手法のクロス参照や論理的整合性の検証が行いやすくなる可能性がある。

背景として、特許分野では既にIBMやGoogle、各国特許庁がAIによる先行技術調査や分類補助に取り組んでおり、近年はLLMを用いたドラフティング支援(例: PatentPalや各種スタートアップのツール)も登場している。一方で、LLM単体ではハルシネーションや請求項特有の文体・依存関係の制御が難しく、グラフベースのグラウンディングとマルチエージェント分業を組み合わせるアプローチは、その弱点を補完する方向性として注目されている。

なお、本論文のURLに含まれるarXiv IDは年代的に整合しない可能性があり、最終的な評価指標や実データセットでの有効性については原文の確認が必要である。実務利用に向けては、法的責任の所在や審査官による評価との整合性といった課題も残ると考えられる。
entries.bodyEn:
Drafting patent claims is one of the most demanding tasks in IP work: the language must capture the essence of an invention with legal precision, neither too broad nor too narrow. IdeaForge proposes a framework that pairs a knowledge graph with multiple LLM agents to analyze innovations across methodologies and automatically generate patent claims.

The central idea appears to be that a single prompted LLM is insufficient for this task. Instead, IdeaForge structures invention concepts, prior art, and relationships between technical domains as an explicit knowledge graph, and lets specialized agents—plausibly handling roles such as retrieval, cross-methodology analysis, claim drafting, and consistency checking—operate over that shared representation. Using the graph as common memory should make it easier to cross-reference techniques from different fields and to verify logical dependencies between independent and dependent claims.

This line of work sits within a broader trend. Patent offices and large companies including the USPTO, EPO, IBM, and Google have invested for years in AI-assisted prior-art search and classification. More recently, LLM-powered drafting assistants from startups such as PatentPal, Solve Intelligence, and Edge have moved into claim and specification generation. The recurring weakness in these tools is that pure LLM pipelines tend to hallucinate references, mishandle antecedent basis, and struggle with the rigid stylistic conventions of claim language. Grounding generation in a knowledge graph and decomposing the workflow across cooperating agents is a plausible way to mitigate those failure modes, echoing similar patterns seen in graph-RAG and agentic research systems.

Cross-methodology analysis is an interesting angle. Much of modern invention happens at the intersection of disciplines—applying a technique from one field to a problem in another. A graph that encodes methods, problems, and domains could in principle surface non-obvious combinations and help draft claims that anticipate variations, although whether IdeaForge actually delivers this in practice would need to be judged from the paper's experiments.

A note of caution: the arXiv identifier shown for this entry looks inconsistent with the stated topic and timeframe, so readers should verify the original paper before citing specific results. Evaluation of patent-drafting systems is also notoriously hard, since quality ultimately depends on examiner reactions, litigation robustness, and downstream commercial value rather than on text-similarity metrics alone.

If the approach holds up, frameworks like IdeaForge could become part of a hybrid workflow where attorneys use AI-generated drafts as a starting point, with the knowledge graph providing traceability for each claim element. Questions around liability, confidentiality of invention disclosures fed into LLMs, and alignment with jurisdiction-specific claim conventions will, however, likely remain central concerns for any real-world deployment.

entries.title: VERA-MH: Validation of Ethical and Responsible AI in Mental Health
entries.titleJa: VERA-MH: メンタルヘルス領域でのAI倫理・責任性評価ベンチマーク
entries.titleEn: VERA-MH: Validation of Ethical and Responsible AI in Mental Health
entries.summaryJa: VERA-MHは、メンタルヘルス用途で利用されるAIシステムの倫理性と責任ある振る舞いを検証するための評価フレームワーク。自殺リスクや危機対応など高リスクシナリオでのLLM応答の安全性を体系的に測定することを目的とする。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chatbot usage has increased, including in fields for which they were never developed for--notably mental health support. To that end, we introduce Valid
entries.bodyJa:
VERA-MH (Validation of Ethical and Responsible AI in Mental Health) は、メンタルヘルス領域に応用されるAIシステム、とりわけ大規模言語モデル (LLM) の倫理的・責任ある振る舞いを検証するために提案された評価フレームワークである。チャットボットや会話型エージェントが心理支援の現場に投入されつつある現在、安全性の体系的な測定手段の必要性が高まっている。

メンタルヘルス用途のAIは、自殺念慮や自傷、虐待の開示など、極めてセンシティブで高リスクな状況に直面しうる。一般的なベンチマークでは、こうした臨床的に重大な場面でのモデルの応答品質を十分に評価できないと指摘されてきた。VERA-MHは、危機対応、共感表現、専門家への適切な紹介 (リファラル)、誤情報の回避といった次元で、モデルの挙動を構造的に検証することを志向していると見られる。

背景には、Woebot や Wysa のようなメンタルヘルス特化型チャットボットの普及に加え、汎用LLMが利用者により事実上のセラピストとして使われている現実がある。米国心理学会 (APA) や各国規制当局も、AIによる心理支援の安全性とエビデンスに関するガイドラインの整備を進めている。NIST AI RMFやEU AI Actが高リスクAIの評価枠組みを求めるなか、ドメイン特化型のベンチマークは政策・実装双方で価値を持つ可能性がある。

技術的には、シナリオベースのテストケース、臨床専門家によるルーブリック評価、自動評価モデル (LLM-as-judge) の組み合わせが採用されるアプローチが一般的であり、VERA-MHも類似の方法論を取ると推察される。課題としては、評価の文化的バイアス、専門家アノテーターの確保コスト、モデル更新に伴うベンチマーク陳腐化などが挙げられる。

なお本論文のarXiv番号は通常の年次採番と異なる形式に見え、詳細な手法や実験結果については原文を直接参照することが望ましい。
entries.bodyEn:
VERA-MH (Validation of Ethical and Responsible AI in Mental Health) is a proposed evaluation framework aimed at validating the ethical and responsible behavior of AI systems, particularly large language models (LLMs), deployed in mental health contexts. As chatbots and conversational agents increasingly enter therapeutic and emotional-support workflows, the need for systematic safety assessment specific to this domain has become acute.

AI tools used in mental health settings inevitably encounter highly sensitive and high-stakes situations: disclosures of suicidal ideation, self-harm, abuse, or acute psychiatric crises. Generic NLP benchmarks rarely capture how models perform in these clinically critical moments. VERA-MH appears designed to address this gap by structurally probing model behavior across dimensions such as crisis response, empathic communication, appropriate referral to human professionals, and avoidance of harmful misinformation or unsafe advice.

The broader context is significant. Dedicated mental health chatbots such as Woebot and Wysa have been used by millions of people, while general-purpose LLMs like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are increasingly used as informal emotional support or de facto therapists, often without clinical oversight. Recent reports of harmful interactions, including cases where chatbots reportedly failed to respond appropriately to suicidal users, have intensified scrutiny from regulators and professional bodies. The American Psychological Association has issued cautions about AI in psychotherapy, and frameworks like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the EU AI Act categorize health-adjacent AI as high-risk, demanding rigorous validation.

Methodologically, domain-specific safety benchmarks of this kind typically combine curated scenario datasets, expert-defined rubrics grounded in clinical guidelines (such as those from the WHO or Zero Suicide initiatives), human expert annotation, and increasingly LLM-as-judge automated scoring. VERA-MH likely follows a similar pattern, though specifics should be confirmed against the source. A robust benchmark in this space must balance reproducibility with the inherent subjectivity of clinical judgment, and ideally cover diverse cultural, linguistic, and demographic contexts since norms around mental health vary widely.

Several challenges remain open for any such effort. Recruiting qualified clinicians as annotators is expensive and slow, limiting dataset scale. Benchmarks can become stale quickly as model providers patch known failure modes, raising concerns about overfitting to a static test set. There is also a risk that benchmark performance becomes a marketing proxy rather than evidence of real-world safety, especially without longitudinal user studies. Comparable initiatives, such as MentalLLM evaluations, the CRISIS benchmark work, and Stanford HAI's responsible AI evaluations, illustrate the growing but still fragmented landscape.

If VERA-MH gains traction, it could serve as a reference point for developers, regulators, and healthcare providers evaluating whether a given model is fit to be deployed in mental health–adjacent products. Readers interested in the precise scenarios, scoring criteria, and empirical results should consult the paper directly, as the framing here is based on the announced scope rather than verified experimental details.

entries.title: Diversity of Extensions in Abstract Argumentation
entries.titleJa: 抽象論証における拡張の多様性に関する研究
entries.titleEn: Diversity of Extensions in Abstract Argumentation
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は抽象論証フレームワークにおける「拡張の多様性」を定式化し、可能な解集合がどれほど多様であるかを定量化する手法を提案する。複数の意味論にわたり多様性指標を分析し、意思決定支援や説明可能AIへの応用可能性を示す。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Argumentation is an important topic of AI for modelling and reasoning about arguments. In abstract argumentation, we consider directed graphs, so-called
entries.bodyJa:
抽象論証(Abstract Argumentation)は、Dungが1995年に提案して以来、非単調推論や法的推論、マルチエージェント間の対話における基盤理論として広く研究されてきた。本論文はその文脈で「拡張(extension)の多様性」という新しい視点を導入し、論証フレームワークが許容する解集合がどれほど多彩であるかを定量化する枠組みを提示している。

論証フレームワークでは、引数(argument)を頂点、攻撃関係(attack)を辺とする有向グラフ上で、grounded、preferred、stable、completeなど複数の意味論に従って「受容可能な引数の集合=拡張」が定義される。同じフレームワークでも採用する意味論や状況によって複数の拡張が併存しうるため、それら拡張同士がどの程度互いに異なるか、あるいは類似しているかを測ることには実務的な意義がある。著者らは集合間距離や情報理論的指標を応用して多様性スコアを定式化し、その性質を理論的に分析していると見られる。

多様性の評価は、説明可能AI(XAI)や意思決定支援の観点で重要性が高まっている。例えば法務AIや医療意思決定支援において、単一の最適解よりも「妥当な代替案がどれだけ存在するか」を提示できることはユーザーの判断を支援する。これはレコメンダーシステムにおける多様性研究や、SATソルバ分野で進む解集合のサンプリング・列挙研究とも通底する話題である。

また、ArgSemSATやμ-toksiaといった論証ソルバが国際コンペICCMA(International Competition on Computational Models of Argumentation)で競っていることを踏まえると、多様性指標は今後評価軸として組み込まれる可能性がある。ただし拡張の列挙自体が一般に計算困難であるため、効率的近似アルゴリズムの開発が実装上の課題となろう。本論文は理論的基盤を整える位置づけであり、後続の経験的検証や応用研究が期待される。
entries.bodyEn:
Abstract argumentation, introduced by Dung in 1995, has become a cornerstone formalism for nonmonotonic reasoning, legal AI, and multi-agent dialogue. This paper opens a relatively underexplored angle on the topic: how diverse are the extensions that a given argumentation framework admits, and how can we measure that diversity in a principled way?

In Dung-style frameworks, arguments form the nodes of a directed graph and attacks form the edges. Different semantics—grounded, preferred, stable, complete, and so on—yield different notions of what counts as an acceptable set of arguments, called an extension. For many frameworks, multiple extensions coexist under a single semantics, representing alternative rational positions one could hold. The authors propose formal measures that quantify how different these coexisting extensions are from one another, drawing on set-distance and information-theoretic ideas, and they appear to analyze the behavior of these measures across the standard semantic families.

Why does this matter? Diversity has become a recurring theme across AI subfields. Recommender systems trade off relevance against diversity to avoid filter bubbles; SAT and ASP communities study solution sampling and enumeration to expose the structure of a problem's solution space; and explainable AI increasingly values presenting users with a spread of viable alternatives rather than a single opaque answer. Bringing the same lens to argumentation is natural: in legal reasoning or clinical decision support, knowing that several substantively different defensible positions exist is often more informative than receiving one verdict.

The work also connects to ongoing competitive benchmarking in the field. The International Competition on Computational Models of Argumentation (ICCMA) has driven the development of solvers such as ArgSemSAT, μ-toksia, and pyglaf, focused largely on credulous and skeptical acceptance or extension enumeration. Diversity metrics could plausibly become a future evaluation dimension, especially as users demand richer explanations. That said, enumerating all extensions is generally intractable—preferred-semantics reasoning sits at the second level of the polynomial hierarchy—so practical adoption will likely require sampling-based approximations or structural shortcuts, much as the SAT community has built #SAT and uniform-sampling tooling on top of decision solvers.

The contribution is best read as a foundational, theoretical step. The framework it sets up invites empirical follow-up: which real-world argumentation corpora exhibit high extension diversity, how do diversity scores correlate with perceived disagreement among human annotators, and can diversity-aware solvers offer better explanations? None of those questions are settled here, but the formal vocabulary the paper introduces seems likely to be useful for posing them. As argumentation increasingly interfaces with large language models—where systems like IBM's Project Debater have explored argument mining at scale—having quantitative handles on the space of reasonable conclusions could prove valuable for grounding LLM outputs in transparent, auditable reasoning structures.

entries.title: Ego2World: Compiling Egocentric Cooking Videos into Executable Worlds for Belief-State Planning
entries.titleJa: Ego2World: 一人称料理映像を実行可能世界に変換し信念状態計画を実現
entries.titleEn: Ego2World: Compiling Egocentric Cooking Videos into Executable Worlds for Belief-State Planning
entries.summaryJa: Ego2Worldは一人称視点の料理動画を解析し、実行可能なシミュレーション世界に変換する手法を提案する。物体やアクションを抽出してPDDL風の表現に落とし込み、信念状態計画によりエージェントが部分観測下で調理タスクを推論・遂行できるようにする。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embodied agents in household environments must plan under partial observation: they need to remember objects, track state changes, and recover when acti
entries.bodyJa:
Ego2Worldは、一人称視点で撮影された料理動画を解析し、エージェントが推論・行動できる実行可能なシミュレーション世界へと「コンパイル」する枠組みを提案する研究である。動画から得られる視覚情報を、計画問題として扱える記号的表現に変換する点が特徴とされる。

具体的には、調理動画に登場する物体、状態変化、人間のアクションを抽出し、PDDLに類する形式の述語と演算子へ落とし込むアプローチが取られていると見られる。これによって、暗黙的な手続き知識を含む長尺の料理タスクが、古典的プランナや学習ベースのエージェントが扱える世界モデルへ変換される。さらに重要なのは、生成された世界が完全観測ではなく、信念状態(belief state)に基づく計画を可能にする点である。冷蔵庫の中身や蓋の下の状態など、観測できない事実を確率的に保持しながら行動選択を行う枠組みは、現実の家庭内タスクに近い問題設定と言える。

背景として、Ego4DやEPIC-KITCHENSといった大規模一人称データセットの整備により、人間の手作業を視覚的に解析する研究が急速に進んでいる。一方、LLMを用いたタスクプランニングや、AI2-THOR・VirtualHomeのようなシミュレーション環境での具現化AI(embodied AI)研究も盛んだが、動画から直接プランニング可能な世界を生成する試みは比較的少ない。Ego2Worldはこれらの潮流を橋渡しする位置づけと考えられる。

応用としては、家庭用ロボットの調理補助、AR/VRでの調理ガイド、データ拡張による方策学習などが想定される。ただし、抽出された記号表現の正確性や、未観測物体の信念分布の妥当性は依然として課題であり、実機展開には追加の検証が必要となる可能性がある。動画理解と記号的計画を結びつける本アプローチは、ニューロシンボリックAIの一例として今後の発展が注目される。
entries.bodyEn:
Ego2World proposes a framework for compiling egocentric cooking videos into executable simulated worlds in which planning agents can reason and act. The central idea is to translate raw first-person visual streams into symbolic representations amenable to classical or learned planning, bridging perception and deliberation in a domain rich with procedural knowledge.

According to the paper, the system appears to extract objects, state changes, and human actions from cooking footage and lift them into PDDL-like predicates and operators. The resulting world captures the structure of long-horizon kitchen tasks, including implicit preconditions such as containers being open or ingredients being prepared. Importantly, the compiled environment supports belief-state planning rather than assuming full observability: hidden contents of fridges, drawers, or covered pots are represented probabilistically, and the agent must choose actions that account for this uncertainty. This setting is much closer to real household robotics than the fully observed toy domains often used in planning benchmarks.

The work sits at the intersection of several active research threads. Large egocentric datasets like Ego4D and EPIC-KITCHENS have spurred rapid progress in fine-grained action recognition and hand-object interaction understanding. In parallel, embodied AI platforms such as AI2-THOR, Habitat, and VirtualHome have become standard testbeds for task planning, often combined with LLM-based planners that emit high-level steps. Yet relatively few efforts attempt to derive a planning-ready, partially observable world directly from human demonstration video. Ego2World can be viewed as a bridge between these communities and as an instance of the broader neuro-symbolic trend, where perception models feed structured representations into symbolic reasoners.

Potential applications include robotic cooking assistants that learn recipes by watching people, AR guidance systems that anticipate the user's next step, and data augmentation pipelines that synthesize training rollouts for policy learning. Belief-state planning is particularly relevant for safety-aware behavior, since an agent that knows what it does not know can choose informative actions such as opening a lid before committing to a stir.

Several caveats are worth flagging. The fidelity of the extracted symbolic schema depends heavily on the underlying detectors and action recognizers, and errors in predicate grounding can cascade through the planner. The probability distributions over unobserved facts also need calibration; otherwise belief updates may be overconfident or pathologically uncertain. Scaling from cooking, which has relatively constrained verbs and tools, to broader household activities will likely require richer ontologies and possibly LLM-assisted schema induction. Even so, the approach offers a concrete recipe for turning human video into something an agent can plan over, and it is likely to influence subsequent work on learning world models from demonstration.

entries.title: Multi-Agent Systems in Emergency Departments: Validation Study on a ED Digital Twin
entries.titleJa: 救急部門のデジタルツインで検証するマルチエージェントAIシステム
entries.titleEn: Multi-Agent Systems in Emergency Departments: Validation Study on a ED Digital Twin
entries.summaryJa: 救急部門(ED)の運用最適化を目的に、デジタルツイン上でマルチエージェントシステム(MAS)を検証した研究。患者・医師・看護師・資源を個別エージェントとしてモデル化し、待ち時間や混雑度の改善効果を定量評価。実病院データに基づくシミュレーションで現実的な意思決定支援への可能性を示す。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emergency departments (ED) face challenges in patient care and resource management. We propose to explore optimization strategies in a realistic and fle
entries.bodyJa:
本論文は、救急部門(Emergency Department, ED)の混雑や待ち時間といった慢性的課題に対し、デジタルツインとマルチエージェントシステム(MAS)を組み合わせて検証したものである。実病院の運用データを用いて構築したED環境の上で、患者・医師・看護師・ベッドや検査機器といった資源それぞれを自律エージェントとして表現し、トリアージから退院までのフローをシミュレートする。

研究の核は「検証(validation)」にあり、MASによるシミュレーション結果が実測の運用指標(在室時間、待ち時間、トリアージ別の処理状況など)とどの程度整合するかを評価している。エージェント間の相互作用と意思決定ルールを変えながら、人員配置や患者振り分けのポリシー変更が全体パフォーマンスに与える影響を分析する枠組みが提示されている。

背景として、EDは需要の急変動・優先度の異なる患者の並行処理・限られた資源という、エージェントベースモデリングが本来得意とする領域である。Anylogic等を用いた離散イベントシミュレーションは以前から医療運用研究で活用されてきたが、近年はLLMを意思決定エージェントに組み込む試みや、病院全体をデジタルツインとして再構築するSiemens HealthineersやGEヘルスケアの取り組みも報告されている。本研究はこうした潮流の中で、MASの再現性と運用判断への応用可能性を実データで検証した点に意義があると見られる。

一方で、エージェントの行動ルールが現実の臨床判断をどこまで近似できるか、稀少イベント(マスカジュアルティ等)への外挿が妥当かといった限界も残る。実装上は政策シミュレータとして有用である可能性が高いが、臨床導入には更なる外部妥当性検証が必要だろう。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper tackles a perennial healthcare operations problem, emergency department (ED) crowding and waiting times, by validating a multi-agent system (MAS) built on top of a digital twin of an ED. Patients, physicians, nurses, and physical resources such as beds and diagnostic equipment are each represented as autonomous agents, and the model simulates the full patient journey from triage through discharge.

The central contribution is validation rather than novelty of architecture. Using operational data from a real hospital, the authors compare simulated outputs (length of stay, waiting time, throughput by triage category) against observed metrics to assess how faithfully the agent-based twin reproduces ED dynamics. With this baseline established, the framework can be used to probe counterfactual scenarios: what happens if staffing schedules shift, if triage policies are tightened, or if patient inflow spikes.

Agent-based modeling has long been a natural fit for the ED setting because of its volatile demand, heterogeneous priorities, and resource contention. Discrete-event simulation tools such as AnyLogic and SimPy have been applied to hospital flow for years, and more recent work in the broader digital twin space, including efforts from Siemens Healthineers and GE HealthCare, has pushed toward whole-hospital virtual replicas. What distinguishes a MAS approach is the explicit representation of decision-making at the level of individual actors, which makes it easier to encode clinical heuristics and to study emergent behavior arising from local interactions.

The study's emphasis on empirical validation is notable because many simulation papers in this domain remain at the conceptual or single-scenario stage. By anchoring the twin to measured KPIs, the authors position the system as a candidate decision-support tool for hospital administrators rather than a purely academic exercise. The framework appears flexible enough to incorporate richer agent policies in the future, and one could imagine layering large language model agents on top to simulate more nuanced clinical reasoning, an emerging direction in healthcare AI research.

Several caveats apply. Rule-based agents necessarily simplify clinical judgment, and validation against one hospital's data does not guarantee transferability to EDs with different case mixes, layouts, or staffing models. Rare but high-impact events such as mass-casualty incidents are particularly difficult to capture with historical calibration alone. The work is best read as a credible step toward operational policy simulators for emergency care, with clinical deployment still requiring broader external validation and likely regulatory scrutiny. Even so, as hospitals face sustained pressure on emergency services, validated MAS-based digital twins may become a practical complement to traditional operations research methods.

entries.title: RS-Claw: Progressive Active Tool Exploration via Hierarchical Skill Trees for Remote Sensing Agents
entries.titleJa: RS-Claw: 階層型スキル木によるリモートセンシングエージェントの能動的ツール探索
entries.titleEn: RS-Claw: Progressive Active Tool Exploration via Hierarchical Skill Trees for Remote Sensing Agents
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はリモートセンシング向けAIエージェントRS-Clawを提案する。階層的なスキルツリー構造を用いて、エージェントが段階的かつ能動的にツールを探索・学習することで、複雑な地理空間タスクへの適応力を高める枠組みである。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rise of multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) is shifting remote sensing (RS) intelligence from "see" to "action", as OpenClaw-style frameworks
entries.bodyJa:
リモートセンシング分野では衛星画像や地理空間データの解析を自動化するAIエージェントへの関心が高まっている。本論文が提案するRS-Clawは、階層的なスキルツリーを通じてエージェントが能動的・段階的にツールを探索する枠組みである。

従来のツール利用型LLMエージェント、たとえばToolformerやReActのようなアプローチでは、利用可能なツール群があらかじめ与えられ、エージェントは状況に応じて選択するに留まることが多い。一方でリモートセンシングの実務では、画像分類、変化検出、物体抽出、地理座標処理など、ツールの粒度や依存関係が複雑であり、単純なフラットなツール一覧では十分に対応しきれないと見られる。

RS-Clawはこの課題に対し、スキルを木構造として階層化し、上位の抽象的な能力から下位の具体的な操作へと探索を進める設計を採る。エージェントはタスクに応じて未知のツールを能動的に試行し、成功した経路をスキルとして蓄積することで、段階的に習熟していく。これによりゼロから全ツールを把握する負荷を抑えつつ、新規タスクへの汎化性を高める狙いがあると考えられる。

関連動向としては、Microsoftの地理空間基盤モデルや、IBMとNASAが共同開発したPrithvi、SegmentAnythingの衛星画像応用など、リモートセンシング向け基盤モデルの整備が進んでいる。RS-Clawのようなエージェント層は、こうしたモデルやGDAL、Google Earth Engineといった既存ツール群を束ねるオーケストレーション基盤として機能する余地がある。

なお本稿で示されたURLは形式的に通常のarXiv論文と異なる可能性があるため、評価指標や実験範囲の詳細は原文での確認が望ましい。能動的探索と階層スキルという発想自体は、汎用エージェント研究の潮流と整合的であり、専門領域への適用例として注目に値する。
entries.bodyEn:
Remote sensing increasingly relies on AI agents to automate analysis of satellite imagery and geospatial data. This paper proposes RS-Claw, a framework in which an agent progressively and actively explores tools organized as a hierarchical skill tree, aiming to handle the complexity of real-world Earth observation workflows.

Most tool-using LLM agents, such as those built on Toolformer or ReAct paradigms, assume a relatively flat catalog of callable tools and focus on selection at inference time. Remote sensing, however, involves a wide variety of operations: scene classification, change detection, semantic segmentation, object extraction, coordinate transformations, and raster-vector conversions. These tools have non-trivial dependencies and varying granularity, which a flat list arguably fails to capture efficiently.

RS-Claw addresses this by structuring skills as a tree, allowing the agent to descend from abstract capabilities to concrete operations as a task demands. Crucially, exploration is described as active and progressive: the agent attempts unfamiliar tools, evaluates outcomes, and consolidates successful trajectories back into its skill repository. This curriculum-like accumulation is intended to reduce the burden of mastering every tool upfront while improving generalization to novel queries, although the exact gains will depend on the experimental setup reported in the paper itself.

The broader ecosystem context is worth noting. Foundation models tailored to Earth observation, such as IBM and NASA's Prithvi, Clay, and Microsoft's geospatial offerings, have matured rapidly, alongside adaptations of Segment Anything for aerial imagery. Tooling stacks like GDAL, rasterio, and platforms such as Google Earth Engine remain the practical backbone of geospatial work. An agent layer like RS-Claw could plausibly serve as an orchestrator that bridges these foundation models and classical tools, deciding which to invoke for a given analytical goal.

Hierarchical skill libraries also echo ideas from general agent research, including Voyager's skill library for Minecraft and various works on automatic curriculum learning. Applying those concepts to a vertical domain with strong spatial priors is a natural and potentially fruitful direction, though the degree to which hierarchy itself, rather than the underlying base model, drives performance is something readers may want to scrutinize.

The URL provided for this submission appears unusual for a standard arXiv listing, so readers should consult the original source to confirm benchmarks, baselines, and ablations. Regardless, the combination of active tool discovery and hierarchical skill organization positions RS-Claw as a notable example of domain-specialized agent design, and it may influence how future remote sensing copilots are architected.

entries.title: TRIAGE: Evaluating Prospective Metacognitive Control in LLMs under Resource Constraints
entries.titleJa: TRIAGE: リソース制約下でのLLMの予測的メタ認知制御を評価
entries.titleEn: TRIAGE: Evaluating Prospective Metacognitive Control in LLMs under Resource Constraints
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はLLMが自身の能力を事前に見積もり、限られた計算・時間資源の中で問題に取り組むかを判断する「予測的メタ認知制御」を評価するベンチマークTRIAGEを提案する。モデルが自信過剰や過小評価をどの程度回避できるかを測定する。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying language models as autonomous agents requires more than per-task accuracy: when an agent faces a queue of problems under a finite token budget
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)の評価は通常、与えられた問題をどれだけ正しく解けるかという「事後的な正答率」に基づくが、現実の運用ではすべての問題に同じ計算資源を割くわけにはいかない。本論文が提案するTRIAGEは、モデルが自身の能力を事前に評価し、限られた資源のもとで「どの問題に取り組むか」を選別する能力、すなわち予測的メタ認知制御を測定するベンチマークである。

TRIAGEのコンセプトは医療現場のトリアージに着想を得ている。モデルは問題集合を提示され、各問題について解くかスキップするかを選択し、選んだ問題のみで採点される。資源制約(時間・トークン・試行回数など)が与えられるため、自信過剰なモデルは難問に取り組んで点を落とし、過度に保守的なモデルは易問まで放棄して機会を失う。理想的なモデルは、自分の正答可能性を正確にキャリブレーションし、期待効用を最大化する問題選択を行うことが求められると見られる。

この評価軸は、近年注目されているLLMのキャリブレーション研究やセルフリフレクション、selective predictionの流れに位置付けられる。OpenAIやAnthropicが安全性評価で重視している「モデルが自分の限界を知る能力(know what you don't know)」とも密接に関連する。また、エージェント設計においては、タスクをサブゴールに分解しコストを見積もる必要があり、TRIAGE的な観点は実用上のエージェント性能にも直結する可能性がある。

注意点として、本記事で参照されているarXiv IDは形式的に未来的な番号であり、論文の実在性や著者情報、具体的な実験結果については確認が必要である。提案手法の有効性や、どのモデルが最も高い予測的メタ認知能力を示したかといった詳細は原典で確認されたい。一般論として、フロンティアモデルほど自己評価精度が向上する傾向が報告されているが、依然として系統的な過信バイアスが残るとの指摘もある。
entries.bodyEn:
Standard LLM benchmarks measure raw accuracy on a fixed set of problems, but real-world deployments rarely afford uniform compute across every query. TRIAGE reframes evaluation around a more operationally relevant question: can a model judge in advance which problems it should attempt and which it should skip, given finite resources?

The benchmark, as its name suggests, borrows its framing from medical triage. A model is shown a batch of problems together with an explicit budget constraint, such as a token, time, or attempt limit. Rather than answering everything, the model must select a subset to engage with, and only those attempted items contribute to its score. An overconfident system wastes its budget on problems it ultimately fails, while an overly cautious one forgoes easy wins. The optimal policy requires accurate self-calibration: estimating per-problem success probability and choosing the set that maximizes expected utility.

This prospective form of metacognition is subtly different from the better-studied post-hoc confidence calibration, where a model rates its certainty after producing an answer. Here the judgment must be made before commitment, more akin to a chess player deciding which lines to even calculate. It is also adjacent to selective prediction and abstention research, but with an added economic dimension: skipping is not free of opportunity cost when other tractable problems exist in the queue.

The research direction connects to several active threads in the field. Anthropic and OpenAI have emphasized that frontier model safety partly depends on models knowing the boundaries of their competence, a property sometimes summarized as knowing what you don't know. Agentic systems built on top of LLMs, such as those orchestrated by frameworks like LangGraph or AutoGen, implicitly rely on similar judgments when deciding whether to invoke a tool, spawn a subagent, or give up on a branch. A reliable TRIAGE-style score could therefore serve as a proxy for downstream agentic robustness, although that mapping has not yet been rigorously established.

Readers should treat the specific claims of this paper with appropriate caution. The arXiv identifier referenced here appears unusual, and the experimental details, including which models were tested and how strongly they exhibited overconfidence or systematic miscalibration, should be verified against the source. As a general empirical pattern, larger and more capable models tend to show better calibration than smaller ones, yet residual overconfidence on out-of-distribution or adversarial items remains a recurring finding across studies. Whether TRIAGE-style evaluation will become a standard companion to accuracy leaderboards likely depends on how well its scores correlate with practical deployment metrics such as cost-adjusted task completion. It is plausible that resource-aware benchmarks of this kind will grow in importance as inference cost becomes a dominant constraint on production LLM use.

entries.title: Cognifold: Always-On Proactive Memory via Cognitive Folding
entries.titleJa: Cognifold: 認知的折り畳みによる常時稼働のプロアクティブ記憶
entries.titleEn: Cognifold: Always-On Proactive Memory via Cognitive Folding
entries.summaryJa: Cognifoldは、LLMエージェント向けに常時稼働するプロアクティブな長期記憶機構を提案する研究である。会話や経験を「認知的折り畳み」と呼ぶ手法で圧縮・階層化し、必要に応じて展開することで、文脈の連続性と能動的な想起を両立させる狙いがある。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing agent memory remains predominantly reactive and retrieval-based, lacking the capacity to autonomously organize experience into persistent cogni
entries.bodyJa:
Cognifoldは、大規模言語モデル(LLM)を用いたエージェントが抱える長期記憶の課題に取り組む研究で、「認知的折り畳み(Cognitive Folding)」と呼ぶ仕組みによって、常時稼働のプロアクティブな記憶を実現することを目指している。

従来のLLMエージェントの記憶は、ベクトル検索によるRAG(Retrieval-Augmented Generation)型が主流であり、ユーザーの問いかけに対して関連情報を引き出す受動的な仕組みであった。これに対しCognifoldは、エージェント側が自発的に過去の経験や文脈を想起し、現在のタスクに関連付ける「プロアクティブ」な動作を志向していると見られる。会話や行動ログを階層的に折り畳んで圧縮し、必要なタイミングで展開する設計により、コンテキストウィンドウの制約を緩和しつつ、長期にわたる一貫性を保つことが意図されている。

背景として、LLMエージェントの記憶設計はここ数年で急速に多様化している。MemGPTのようなOSライクな仮想メモリ管理、LangChainやLlamaIndexが提供する会話バッファやサマリーメモリ、さらにLettaやZepのような専用メモリ基盤など、エコシステムは厚みを増している。Cognifoldが提案する「折り畳み」のメタファーは、タンパク質のフォールディングや人間の記憶圧縮プロセスを連想させるもので、単なる要約ではなく階層的な再構成を重視している可能性がある。

一方で、常時稼働の記憶機構は計算コストやプライバシー、想起のノイズといった課題を伴う。エージェントが過剰に過去を参照すれば、ハルシネーションや誤った文脈の混入を招きかねない。論文の主張する有効性が、どの程度の規模や領域で再現可能なのかは今後の検証が待たれるところだろう。AIエージェントの自律性と長期運用が重要視される現状において、この種の記憶アーキテクチャ研究は注目に値する方向性と言える。
entries.bodyEn:
Cognifold is a research proposal that tackles one of the most persistent problems in LLM-based agents: how to maintain useful long-term memory across extended interactions. The authors introduce a mechanism they call cognitive folding, intended to support an always-on, proactive form of memory rather than the reactive retrieval pattern that dominates today.

Most current LLM agents rely on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) style memory, where past content is embedded into a vector store and pulled back only when the user asks something that triggers a similarity match. This is fundamentally reactive: the agent does not remember unless prompted. Cognifold appears to flip this model. By continuously folding conversations, observations, and actions into hierarchical, compressed representations, the agent can unfold relevant slices of its own history on its own initiative, weaving prior context into ongoing reasoning without waiting for an explicit query.

The folding metaphor is evocative. It echoes both protein folding, where structure emerges from compact arrangements, and theories of human memory consolidation, where episodic traces are progressively abstracted into schemas. Rather than flat summarization, the approach seems to emphasize layered reorganization: low-level details can remain accessible by unfolding deeper, while higher-level gist serves day-to-day reasoning. This may help mitigate the context window bottleneck that still constrains even frontier models, while preserving coherence over weeks or months of interaction.

The broader ecosystem around agent memory has matured quickly. MemGPT pioneered an OS-inspired view of paging information in and out of the working context. Frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex ship buffer, summary, and entity memory modules out of the box. Dedicated memory services such as Letta, Zep, and mem0 offer hosted long-term stores, and recent research explores graph-structured or episodic memory layers. Cognifold positions itself in this landscape by emphasizing the always-on, proactive dimension, which has been less explored than retrieval quality or storage backends.

That said, proactive memory introduces its own risks. An agent that constantly references prior states can amplify hallucinations, inject stale or irrelevant context, and incur nontrivial compute costs at every turn. Privacy is another concern: persistent personal histories raise questions about retention, consent, and deletion that product teams will need to address before such systems reach end users. The strength of the empirical evaluation, and how well the approach generalizes beyond the benchmarks chosen by the authors, will likely determine how much traction the idea gains.

Still, the direction feels timely. As agentic systems move from single-turn assistants to long-running collaborators handling multi-day projects, memory architecture is becoming as important as the underlying model. Proposals like Cognifold suggest that the field is starting to treat memory not as a bolt-on retrieval layer but as a first-class cognitive component, one that may need its own structural primitives rather than borrowed database patterns.

entries.title: Assessing the Creativity of Large Language Models: Testing, Limits, and New Frontiers
entries.titleJa: 大規模言語モデルの創造性評価:テスト、限界、新たな地平
entries.titleEn: Assessing the Creativity of Large Language Models: Testing, Limits, and New Frontiers
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は大規模言語モデル(LLM)の創造性を評価する枠組みを提案し、既存の創造性テストをLLMに適用してその能力と限界を検証する。創造的タスクにおける性能の傾向と今後の研究方向を議論している。
entries.summaryEn: arXiv:2605.13450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measuring the creativity of large language models (LLMs) is essential for designing methods that can improve creativity and for enhancing our scientific
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)の能力評価は、当初の言語理解や推論タスクから、より人間らしい能力である「創造性」へと拡張されつつある。本論文はその潮流の中で、LLMの創造性をどのように測定すべきかという問いに正面から取り組んでいる。

著者らは、心理学分野で長年用いられてきた創造性評価手法をLLMに適用することを試みる。代表的な手法には、ある物の代替的な用途を列挙させるAlternative Uses Test (AUT) や、関連性の薄い単語をつなぐ概念を答えさせるRemote Associates Test (RAT) などがあり、流暢性・柔軟性・独自性・精緻性といった次元から創造的思考を測定するのが一般的である。本研究ではこれらをLLMに適用し、人間との比較や限界の所在を整理していると見られる。

結果として、LLMは既存知識の組み合わせや拡散的思考の一部タスクで高いスコアを示す一方、真に独自性のあるアイデアや、文脈に強く依存する収束的思考では人間に及ばない場面が残る可能性が示唆される。これは、LLMが訓練データの統計的分布に強く依存し、分布外の発想を生み出しにくい構造的特徴と関連していると考えられる。

関連する動向として、OpenAIやGoogle DeepMindなどはモデルの「創造的執筆」性能を強調するベンチマークを整備しつつあり、研究コミュニティでもLLM-as-a-judge方式やヒューマン評価を組み合わせたアプローチが広がっている。一方で、創造性の定義そのものが多義的であるため、評価指標の標準化は依然として課題である。本論文は、LLM時代における創造性研究の枠組み構築に向けた一歩と位置づけられる。
entries.bodyEn:
Evaluating large language models has steadily expanded from narrow benchmarks of language understanding and reasoning toward more distinctly human capacities, with creativity being one of the most contested. This paper engages directly with the question of how to measure creativity in LLMs and what such measurements can, and cannot, tell us.

The authors draw on a long tradition of creativity assessment from psychology. Tools such as the Alternative Uses Test (AUT), which asks subjects to list unconventional uses for an everyday object, and the Remote Associates Test (RAT), which probes the ability to connect distantly related concepts, have for decades been used to quantify divergent and convergent thinking. Standard scoring dimensions include fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration. The paper appears to adapt these instruments to LLMs, comparing model outputs against human baselines and probing where the analogy holds and where it breaks down.

The broad pattern that emerges, as far as can be inferred, is that LLMs perform competitively on tasks that reward recombination of existing knowledge and broad associative recall. They tend to be fluent and flexible, often producing more candidate ideas than a typical human respondent. However, their performance on tasks requiring genuinely novel insights, strong contextual grounding, or convergent problem solving with a uniquely correct creative leap remains uneven. This is consistent with what we would expect from systems whose outputs are shaped by the statistical structure of their training data, which can make truly out-of-distribution ideation difficult.

The paper also raises methodological concerns that the field has yet to settle. Originality, for instance, is usually scored against a reference population, and it is unclear how to fairly score an LLM whose training corpus may already contain large portions of that reference space. Prompt sensitivity, sampling temperature, and decoding strategy can all materially shift creativity scores, raising questions about reproducibility. The authors suggest that future work needs both more robust protocols and creativity tests designed specifically with LLMs in mind, rather than borrowed wholesale from human psychometrics.

The broader ecosystem context is worth noting. Frontier labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind have increasingly highlighted creative writing and ideation benchmarks in their model releases, and community efforts such as LLM-as-a-judge evaluations, human preference studies, and specialized arenas for creative tasks are proliferating. Yet because creativity itself is a contested, multidimensional construct, no single benchmark has achieved consensus status comparable to MMLU or GSM8K in their respective domains.

Viewed in that light, the contribution of this paper is less a definitive verdict on whether LLMs are creative and more a careful mapping of the conceptual and empirical terrain. It offers a vocabulary and a set of instruments that other researchers can build on, while flagging the limits of applying human-centered tests to systems whose cognitive substrate is fundamentally different. As LLMs continue to be deployed in writing, design, and research workflows, such evaluative groundwork is likely to grow in practical, and not merely academic, importance.

entries.title: AI-Generated Slides: Are They Good? Can Students Tell?

entries.titleEn: AI-Generated Slides: Are They Good? Can Students Tell?
entries.summaryJa: AIが自動生成したプレゼンスライドの品質を評価し、学生が人間制作のスライドと見分けられるかを調査した研究。生成AIを教育現場で活用する際の妥当性や、視覚的・内容的な差異の有無を実証的に検討している。

entries.bodyJa:
生成AIが文章や画像のみならず、プレゼンテーション資料の自動作成にも応用されつつある中、本研究はAIが生成したスライドの品質と、それを学生が人間作のものと区別できるかという二つの問いに取り組んでいる。教育現場でのAI活用を考える上で示唆に富むテーマである。

研究では、同一トピックについて人間とAIがそれぞれスライドを作成し、レイアウト、文章の的確さ、視覚デザイン、内容の網羅性といった観点から比較評価を行ったと見られる。さらに学生を被験者として、どちらがAI製かを当てさせるブラインドテストを実施し、識別精度を測定するアプローチを取っている。こうした手法はチューリングテスト的な発想に近く、AI出力の「自然さ」を測る指標として近年広く採用されている。

背景には、Gamma、Beautiful.ai、Microsoft Copilot for PowerPoint、Googleスライドの Duet AI など、スライド自動生成ツールの急速な普及がある。これらは見出し構成からビジュアル選定までを一括で処理し、教員や学生の作業負担を大きく減らす可能性がある一方、内容の正確性やオリジナリティ、引用の妥当性といった教育上の懸念も指摘されてきた。

仮にAI製スライドが人間製と区別困難であれば、教育評価や著作権、学習効果の測定方法を見直す必要が出てくる可能性がある。逆に明確な差が残るなら、AIをドラフト生成役に限定し、人間が仕上げるハイブリッド運用が現実的だろう。本研究のような実証データは、ガイドライン策定や授業設計を考える教育者にとって有用な基礎資料となり得る。

なお本稿で参照しているURLのarXiv IDは形式的に通常範囲外であり、論文の実在性や詳細についてはオリジナルを確認する必要がある点には留意したい。
entries.bodyEn:
As generative AI expands beyond text and images into automated creation of presentation materials, this study tackles two related questions: how good are AI-generated slides, and can students tell them apart from human-made ones? The topic is increasingly relevant for educators weighing AI adoption in classrooms.

The research reportedly compares slides produced by humans and AI on the same topics, evaluating layout, textual accuracy, visual design, and content coverage. It then runs a blind test in which students attempt to identify which deck was machine-generated, measuring discrimination accuracy. The setup resembles a Turing-style evaluation, an approach that has become common for benchmarking the perceived naturalness of generative model output across modalities.

The context matters. Tools like Gamma, Beautiful.ai, Tome, Microsoft Copilot for PowerPoint, and Google Slides' Duet AI integration have rapidly matured, offering one-click generation of structured decks complete with imagery and speaker notes. For students and instructors, these promise significant time savings on routine slide assembly. However, concerns persist around factual accuracy, citation handling, originality, and whether reliance on such tools undermines the pedagogical value of preparing presentations in the first place.

If AI-produced slides are indistinguishable from human ones, institutions may need to revisit how presentations are graded and how academic integrity policies are framed, much as they have for AI-written essays. Conversely, if reviewers can still spot tell-tale signs, such as generic stock imagery, formulaic bullet patterns, or shallow argumentation, a hybrid workflow becomes more defensible: AI handles drafting and formatting, while students contribute critical thinking, synthesis, and domain-specific insight.

From a broader research perspective, slide generation is a useful testbed because it combines multiple AI capabilities at once, including text summarization, layout reasoning, image selection, and discourse structuring. Weaknesses in any of these dimensions tend to surface in the final artifact, which makes human perception studies a relatively efficient way to probe overall system quality without needing complex automated metrics.

Readers should treat specific findings cautiously until the underlying paper is consulted directly, as the cited identifier appears unusual and details could not be independently verified here. Still, the framing of the work points to a productive line of inquiry. As more coursework, conference talks, and corporate briefings are partially or fully drafted by AI, empirical evidence on perceived quality and detectability will help shape sensible guidelines, rather than leaving the question to anecdote.

It is plausible that results will mirror trends seen in AI-written text studies, where non-expert readers struggle to identify machine output on short, well-scoped tasks, while domain experts retain an edge on nuanced material. If so, the practical takeaway for educators may be less about banning AI slide tools and more about designing assessments that emphasize the parts of presentation work, such as live delivery, Q and A, and reasoning depth, that current generative systems cannot easily replicate.

entries.title: Scaling Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Parallel Search and Explicit Merging
entries.titleJa: 並列検索と明示的マージで検索拡張推論をスケールさせる新手法
entries.titleEn: Scaling Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Parallel Search and Explicit Merging
entries.summaryJa: 検索拡張推論を強化するため、複数のクエリを並列実行し結果を明示的にマージする手法を提案。逐次的な検索の依存関係を断ち切り、長い推論チェーンでの効率とスケーラビリティを高めると報告されている。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a retrieval-augmented reasoning framework that issues searches in parallel and merges results explicitly, aiming to improve scalability and efficiency over sequential search-and-reason loops in long reasoning chains.
entries.bodyJa:
本論文は、大規模言語モデル(LLM)による検索拡張推論(retrieval-augmented reasoning)を、並列検索と明示的なマージ操作によってスケールさせる手法を提案している。検索と推論を交互に繰り返す既存手法のボトルネックを解消することを狙いとしている。

従来のReActやSearch-R1のようなフレームワークでは、LLMが次に何を検索するかを逐次的に決定し、得られた情報を踏まえて次の推論ステップへ進む。この逐次性は推論の一貫性を保ちやすい一方で、ステップ数が増えるほどレイテンシが累積し、誤った中間結論が後続の検索を歪める「経路依存性」の問題も抱える。本論文の手法は、複数の検索クエリを同時に発行し、得られた結果を明示的なマージ段階で統合することで、これらの課題に対処すると見られる。

技術的には、クエリ分解、並列実行、そして結果の重複排除や矛盾解消を担うマージ演算子の設計が鍵となる。これは古典的なMapReduceや、近年のTree-of-ThoughtsやGraph-of-Thoughtsといった非線形推論の系譜とも親和性が高い。エージェント型RAGの文脈では、LangGraphやLlamaIndexのクエリエンジンでも並列サブクエリは実装例があるが、本研究はそれを学習や評価のレベルで体系化する試みと位置付けられる可能性がある。

マルチホップQAや複雑な調査タスクでは、必要な情報が複数のドキュメントに分散しているため、並列探索の恩恵が大きいと期待される。一方で、並列度を上げるほど検索コストやノイズ混入のリスクも増えるため、マージ品質と計算コストのトレードオフが実運用上の論点になると考えられる。

なお提示されたURLのarXiv IDは形式的に違和感があり、最新の関連研究を参照する際は原典の確認を推奨する。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper proposes a framework for scaling retrieval-augmented reasoning in large language models by issuing search queries in parallel and combining their results through an explicit merging step. The goal is to overcome the bottlenecks of sequential search-and-reason loops that dominate current agentic RAG systems.

In established approaches such as ReAct or Search-R1, the model decides what to look up next based on prior retrieval results, alternating between thought and action. While this preserves coherence, it accumulates latency with every hop and introduces a kind of path dependence: an early erroneous inference can derail subsequent queries. By decomposing a question into multiple sub-queries that run concurrently and then consolidating their evidence, the proposed method aims to reduce wall-clock cost and limit the propagation of mistakes across reasoning steps.

The technical core appears to involve query decomposition, parallel retrieval execution, and a merge operator that handles deduplication, conflict resolution, and aggregation across heterogeneous evidence. Conceptually this echoes the MapReduce pattern as well as more recent non-linear reasoning structures such as Tree-of-Thoughts and Graph-of-Thoughts, where branching exploration is followed by a synthesis stage. Practical agent frameworks like LangGraph and LlamaIndex already support parallel sub-queries at the orchestration level, but the contribution here seems to lie in formalizing the approach so it can be trained for and evaluated systematically, rather than treated purely as a prompt-engineering pattern.

Multi-hop question answering and deep research style tasks are the most natural beneficiaries, since the evidence needed to answer is typically spread across many documents and does not require strict ordering to be gathered. Parallel retrieval can shorten the critical path significantly and is well-aligned with how human researchers fan out searches before drawing conclusions. That said, increasing parallel breadth raises retrieval cost and the risk of noisy or contradictory passages entering the context window, so the design of the merging stage—how it weighs sources, resolves conflicts, and prunes irrelevant snippets—is likely decisive for end-to-end accuracy.

It is also worth noting that the arXiv identifier provided in the source link looks unusual for a current preprint, so readers interested in citing or reproducing the work should verify the canonical reference directly. Regardless of the specific paper, the broader direction of trading sequential depth for parallel breadth in retrieval-augmented reasoning is an active research theme, and we are likely to see more systems combining learned query planners with explicit aggregation modules in the near future.
